title: Staff Data Platform Software Engineer - veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem  across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources  providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance. 

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents.  For engineers joining Veza today, this means the scale and resources of an enterprise platform company, with the product velocity and mission-driven focus of a security innovator at a pivotal moment in the industry.

Job Description

We are looking for a passionate Staff Software Engineer to join Veza's Graph Data Platform team. You will play a key role in designing, improving, and maintaining the robust and scalable code behind the Veza Access Graph, collaborating closely with cross-functional teams to shape the future of our products and deliver exceptional identity and access management experiences to our customers. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the growth and success of a high-impact team while working on cutting-edge technologies.

What You Will Do

Technical Leadership

  • Act as the technical expert for the Veza Access Graph, identifying broad challenges — technical, functional, or business — and parsing them into initiatives the org can execute against
  • Solve complex problems with no established precedent in the org or the field, from architecture through implementation
  • Serve as the dependable subject-matter expert (SME) for your area; define coding standards and engineering best practices for the team
  • Identify opportunities to simplify systems, reduce redundancy, and drive large-scale simplification across the platform
  • Deliver significant direct technical contributions while independently driving workstream-level design reviews
  • Set the bar for code quality, testing, documentation, and support — and share best practices with teammates in a consumable format

Roadmap & Execution

  • Set roadmap and prioritization for workstreams in your area; drive planning, design, and delegation of key components to ICs and stakeholders
  • Identify gaps, dependencies, and unresolved problems; partner with customers and stakeholders to close them
  • Proactively refine technical requirements in alignment with key stakeholders
  • Operate autonomously, consistently delivering high-quality work on time

Collaboration & Mentorship

  • Break complex roadmaps into clear workstreams, milestones, and timelines, driving alignment and buy-in across PMs, TPMs, EMs, TLs, ICs, and dependency teams
  • Represent your team's roadmap and dependencies in company-wide initiatives
  • Coach and mentor team leads and ICs; help define interview loops, identify talent gaps, and build coaching plans to close them
  • Drive collaboration, conflict resolution, and stakeholder buy-in to unblock projects and ensure successful delivery
  • Model ServiceNow's core values and contribute feedback to improve team culture

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of professional backend software development experience, with a focus on scalable distributed systems, data management, identity, security, or related domains
  • Distributed systems fundamentals — consistency models, partitioning/sharding, replication, consensus, failure modes at scale
  • Graph database internals — traversal algorithms, query planning/optimization, indexing strategies (not just querying an existing graph API)
  • Go at a systems-programming level — concurrency patterns, memory/performance tuning, and production experience building and testing backend services
  • Large-scale data modeling — schema design for graphs handling high cardinality/fan-out
  • Experience designing and implementing RESTful APIs in microservice architectures
  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and containerization / orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes)
  • Familiarity with caching mechanisms in distributed systems
  • Track record of technical decisions with org-wide blast radius — not just execution within an assigned mandate
  • Experience setting technical direction or standards adopted by multiple teams
  • Systems design for correctness and rollback safety in high-stakes infrastructure (access/identity data qualifies)
  • Fluency with AI-assisted engineering — using LLM-based tools (Claude Code, Copilot, or similar) to accelerate design exploration, code review, debugging, and documentation, while knowing when to trust generated output versus verifying it against source, tests, or runtime behavior

Nice to have:

  • Storage engine or query engine experience — having built or deeply modified one (Neo4j internals or a comparable engine)
  • Deep knowledge of relational algebra and graph algorithms, with experience across OLTP and OLAP systems
  • Track record of using AI tools to multiply personal and team output on complex, large-codebase work — beyond autocomplete-level usage
  • Identity and access management concepts (RBAC/ABAC, permission graphs, entitlement modeling)
  • Security or compliance-adjacent engineering background
  • Graduate degree

You Are:

  • A rigorous problem-solver who instinctively verifies assumptions rather than guessing — you dig into logs, code, and system behavior before proposing a fix, and you're comfortable being wrong in public if it gets the team to the right answer faster.
  • Someone who thrives with ambiguity: you can take a vague mandate ("make the graph queries faster," "harden this for scale") and turn it into a scoped plan with clear tradeoffs, then execute it independently — while knowing exactly when to loop others in.
  • A systems thinker who considers blast radius and reversibility before making changes to critical infrastructure — especially in a domain like ours, where a subtle bug in the access graph has real security consequences.
  • A strong communicator who can explain why a traversal algorithm is O(n²) to another engineer and why that matters for customer-facing latency to a product manager — without losing precision or condescending to either audience.
  • Fluent with AI as a working tool, not a crutch — you use it to move faster through exploration, boilerplate, and first drafts, but you still own the correctness of what ships, and you can tell the difference between "the model sounds confident" and "this is actually verified."
  • Someone who treats AI-assisted output the same way you'd treat a junior engineer's PR — useful, often good, but reviewed with the same rigor as anything else before it touches production.
  • A mentor who multiplies the team's effectiveness, not just your own — you review code like you're teaching, you pair when it helps someone level up, and you measure your impact partly by how the engineers around you grow.
  • Someone who leaves things better than you found them: documentation, test coverage, runbooks, and team practices all improve because you touched them.
  • Low-ego and high-trust — you can disagree strongly in a design review and still buy the team a round after it's decided.
  • A pleasure to work with — even at 2am during an incident.

ServiceNow’s Applied AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team is where bold ideas meet transformative action. We partner with our most strategic customers to shape the future of enterprise AI. Together, we identify high-value opportunities, accelerate business outcomes, and build reusable AI-native solutions that advance the Now AI Platform. 

Our mission: We partner deeply with our customers to build intelligent, scalable AI solutions that solve their most mission-critical challenges. By embedding in real-world complexity, we deliver fast, iterate with purpose, and transform every success into reusable patterns that accelerate transformation across the Now Platform and the broader enterprise. 

Why This Role Matters:

Enterprises are raising the bar. AI initiatives must deliver business value—not just promise potential. That means taking cutting-edge LLM capabilities and turning them into resilient, secure, and scalable software. 

As a Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE), you act as the CTO of the build—owning everything from backend services to LLM pipelines and front-end integrations. You partner with customers in the field to design, implement, and deliver solution-ready builds in agile sprints. Your software becomes the reference implementation for scalable GenAI in the enterprise. You codify patterns, shape internal tooling, and accelerate innovation—delivering systems that are battle-tested in production and scalable across industries. 

Who You Are:

You are a systems-minded, AI-native engineer who ships real software. You own the full stack—and are equally motivated by elegant APIs, intuitive UIs, and scalable orchestration pipelines. You think like a product-minded CTO, balancing creativity with pragmatism to deliver impact. 

You embed deeply with customer teams, diagnose root problems, and architect AI-powered workflows that run at scale. You don’t just debug code—you debug systems, context, and customer pain points. 

You will: 

  • Build solution-ready LLM-enabled applications that span backend logic, data orchestration, and front-end UI 
  • Operate in the field, working side-by-side with customers to adapt, deploy, and iterate in live environments 
  • Codify reusable assets—libraries, prompts, scaffolds—to accelerate future engagements 
  • Shape developer experience by sharing feedback with platform and product teams

  • Deliver Production - readysolution in agile end-to-end sprints
  • Engineer with versatility: APIs, orchestration pipelines, vector DBs, LLM frameworks, UI components 
  • Operate with agility: integrate with legacy systems, navigate ambiguity, ship safely at speed 
  • Codify patterns: build scaffolds, SDKs, and documentation to scale success across customers 
  • Influence platform: inform product strategy through field-tested insights and extensible code 

What Success Looks Like:

  • Production-grade delivery: Your solution builds consistently convert to scaled deployments in production environments 
  • Reusable impact: You author libraries, prompts, and scaffolds that power multiple deployments and projects 
  • Platform influence: Your work shapes internal tooling and is integrated into platform roadmap and primitives 
  • Velocity and precision: You move fast without breaking things—shaping resilient, secure systems in high-stakes contexts 
  • Engineering leadership: You are trusted by architects, PMs, and customer teams to lead implementation from zero to one 

Qualifications

What You Bring:

  • Experience: In leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry
  • Relevant Experience: 10+ years of software engineering, including 2+ years building systems in customer-facing or embedded roles 
  • System architecture: Proven ability to design and implement AI-native software in production environments 
  • Engineering depth: Strength in backend (Python, Node.js, Java), frontend (React, Angular), APIs (REST/GraphQL) 
  • Machine Learning: Foundations of MLflow, Weights & Biases, LoRA, PEFT, SageMaker, Vertex AI, AzureML, Kubeflow, Airflow, Prefect, TorchServe, Triton, vLLM, SHAP, LIME, pandas, Spark, SQL
  • LLM tooling: Familiarity with LangChain, Semantic Kernel, prompt chaining, vector search, and context management 
  • Performance & observability: Skilled in debugging distributed systems, tuning for latency, and implementing monitoring 
  • Platform mindset: Can contribute to shared SDKs and tools, raising engineering velocity for the whole org 
  • Product sensibility: Prioritize for user value, MVP iteration, and long-term scale 
  • DevOps fluency: Experience deploying in AWS, Azure, or GCP with CI/CD, containers, and infra-as-code 
  • Field readiness: Able to travel up to 30% to embed onsite and deliver where it matters 

Preferred Qualifications:

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Integrations (Tech Lead) — Veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem  across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources  providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance. 

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents.  For engineers joining Veza today, this means the scale and resources of an enterprise platform company, with the product velocity and mission-driven focus of a security innovator at a pivotal moment in the industry.

We are looking for a passionate Senior Staff (Tech Lead) Software Engineer who will play a key role in designing, developing, and maintaining product features of our IAM platform for our Integrations. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to implement robust and scalable solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. 
The Integrations team builds the services which ingest data from external integrations (e.g. AWS, Okta) into the Veza platform, enabling Veza's suite of next-gen features across our wide and growing array of supported integrations. Job Description

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO) delivers world-class, innovative security solutions to reduce risk and protect the company and our customers. We enable our customers to migrate their most sensitive data and workloads to the cloud, accelerating our business so that we are the most trusted SaaS provider. We create an environment where our employees are proud to work and can make a positive impact. 

We are committed to fostering an environment where our employees feel empowered, take pride in their work, and have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact.  

About the Team – Global Security Support Center (GSSC)  

The Global Security Support Center (GSSC) at ServiceNow is a diverse and highly skilled team of security professionals who play a pivotal role in strengthening both our internal and external security posture. The team collaborates closely with various functions across the company and serves as a key interface with our customers on security-related matters.  

Through expertise, communication, and a commitment to excellence, the GSSC team reinforces ServiceNow's reputation as a security-first organization, consistently demonstrating our commitment to protecting our platform, our data, and our customers.  

GSSC Mission Statement: To provide external & internal facing security support on behalf of the Security Organization to improve our customers' security posture and build Customer trust.  

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Represent security organization in customer-facing Security Incidents, cases, Security findings, tasks, questions and calls related to Security & Privacy.  
  • Own, triage, investigate and respond to security matters of the ServiceNow platform, ensuring timely communication, resolution and enhanced customer experience and processes.  
  • Act as the primary point of contact for all security-related matters in ServiceNow, supporting both internal and external stakeholders.  
  • Facilitate the efficient workflow/triage of security-related incidents/cases by collaborating with customers and other internal ServiceNow teams.  
  • Build and maintain a high level of customer trust and confidence through exceptional service and communication.  
  • Manage customer outreach communications on Security & escalation handling.  
  • Understand and deliver excellent capability maturity models to fine-tune security processes.  
  • Create and enhance documentation and processes to strengthen security maturity and operational excellence.  
  • Develop and deliver training/enablement programs on Security, for internal and external customers on security awareness and best practices.  
  • Develop AI Solutions for automating repetitive activities & design new solutions leveraging AI.  
  • Work with Legal on security/privacy-related matters & a global team spread across different time zones, so flexibility of times is required.  
  • Provide support and be available as a responsible resource for the On-Call rotation (weekends, public holidays, and after hours) as rostered.  
  • This role may require access to a Protected B cloud environment. The successful candidate must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Government of Canada Reliability Status under PSPC's Contract Security Program. Clearance is a condition of employment in this function. The company will sponsor and support the screening process through its designated Company Security Officer. 

To be successful in this role, you have: 

  • A minimum of 8 years of professional experience in information security or application security roles. Or similar experience with education 
  • Candidate must be eligible to obtain and hold a reliability status in Canada. 
  • Preferred Certifications (Two or more)  
  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) 
  • Azure AI Fundamentals  
  • AWS Certified AI Practitioner  
  • Offensive Security Web Assessor (OSWA)  
  • GIAC Web Application Penetration Tester (GWAPT)  
  • GIAC Security Essentials Certification (GSEC)  
  • GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH)  
  • CISSP  
  • CISM  

Qualifications

Technical Skills: 

  • Solid understanding of cloud computing models and major hyperscaler cloud models.  
  • Hands-on experience with using and understanding security tools and technologies, including: SIEM solutions, logging tools, load balancers, firewalls, WAFs, IDS/IPS, vulnerability management platforms, encryption techniques, etc.  
  • Basic to Intermediate-level programming knowledge in Java/JavaScript with the ability to read, interpret & understand to explain code effectively.  
  • Intermediate to Advanced proficiency in using web proxy tools for security testing and assessments.  
  • Application Security: In-depth understanding of web application vulnerabilities (e.g., OWASP Top Ten) and corresponding mitigation strategies.  
  • Risk Management: Ability to clearly explain security risks to non-technical stakeholders using straightforward, non-technical language.  
  • Compliance & Regulatory Knowledge: Good knowledge of key compliance and regulatory frameworks including: NIST, CIS, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO standards, etc.  
  • Artificial Intelligence: Experience working with AI technologies and designing AI-based solutions.  
  • Analytical Thinking: Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to evaluate and address complex security challenges.  

Soft Skills & Communication:  

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey technical information to a non-technical audience.  
  • Demonstrated ability to thrive in a team-oriented, collaborative environment, working in a follow-the-sun model.  
  • Good understanding of Security concepts and articulating Security and risk in simple terms without using jargon that makes sense to customers.  

Education & Experience: 

  • Preferred Bachelor's degree in computer science or information security or relevant information security experience.  
  • Preferred: Hands-on experience with web-based vulnerability exploitation is a strong plus for success in this role.

title: Sr Software Engineer - Agent Identity Security - Veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem  across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources  providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance. 

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents.  For engineers joining Veza today, this means the scale and resources of an enterprise platform company, with the product velocity and mission-driven focus of a security innovator at a pivotal moment in the industry.

Job Description

About the Team  

We are looking for a passionate Senior Software Engineer, Backend who will play a key role in designing, developing, and maintaining the next frontier of Agent Identity Security. The team is advancing Agent Identity Security as AI agents and copilots rapidly expand across enterprise systems. The team drives innovation, defines next-generation IGA for non-human identities and agents, and helps shape new industry standards as the AI agent ecosystem evolves. Its work includes discovering agents, tracking their actions, and defining access management and runtime authorization capabilities to maintain a strong security posture.  

Your core focus areas:  

  • In this role, you will tackle the unique access risks posed by AI agents, contributing to a high-impact startup at the cutting edge of Identity and Access Management. This is an exciting opportunity where your key responsibilities will include: 
  • Architect and Build: Design, develop, and scale a comprehensive identity security solution for AI agents, ensuring it can manage a diverse landscape of agents deployed across different applications and systems. 
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with product management, other engineering teams, and security experts to translate complex security challenges into robust, scalable, and production-grade features. 
  • End-to-End Ownership: Take ownership of the entire feature lifecycle, from initial concept and design through to deployment, monitoring, and maintenance. 
  • AI-Driven Engineering: Leverage AI techniques and tools to advance and strengthen Agent Security product. 

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. 
  • Experience: Proven 3+ yrs in backend software development, with a focus on APIs, Microservices Architecture or related areas 
  • Strong proficiency in one or more programming languages, such as Golang, Java. 
  • Experience designing and implementing RESTful APIs and Microservices Architectures. 
  • Experience with cloud platforms, such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform, and familiarity with IAM services and features. 
  • Innate love for Distributed Systems (designing, developing, debugging, monitoring) 

Nice to Have: 

  • Experience with Containerization and Orchestration technologies, such as Docker and Kubernetes, is a plus. 
  • Knowledge of database technologies (SQL and NoSQL), caching mechanisms, and distributed systems. 
  • Excellent problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
  • Strong sense of Product feature Ownership – from Ideation to Deployment

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team 

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning. 

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We’re building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability—where an attacker could realistically get in—rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and this role helps define what good looks like. 

The role 

As a Senior Staff Engineer, you own the architecture of an security harness with novel exploitability engine end to end, and you’re accountable for the decisions that shape everything downstream. You set technical direction, make the hard calls defensible, and multiply the engineers around you. 

What you’ll own 

  • The end-to-end architecture of the exploitability engine—from evidence ingestion and entity resolution, through the attack-path probability core and choke-point ranking, to the validation loop that keeps predictions honest. 
  • The decisions that cascade through the system: calibrated probability versus ordinal rank, identity as a first-class graph edge, assume-breach seeding, and how the most critical assets are defined. These are model-shaping calls, not implementation details. 
  • The probabilistic ranking core: edge-traversal probability, guided path search with hop and likelihood limits, correlated-control-failure modeling, and honest uncertainty bands. 
  • The calibration and validation loop—canaries, purple-team and incident replay, calibration measured by zone and vector—that turns modeled weights into evidence rather than opinion. 
  • Make-or-break metrics as first-class engineering targets, starting with entity-resolution accuracy and calibration quality. 
  • The build-on strategy—extending the existing portfolio rather than rebuilding it, and knowing precisely what to reuse and what must be net-new. 

What you’ll do 

  • Lead zero-to-one work at production scale: turn an ambiguous, novel problem into a reliable system other teams build on, and set the bar where no precedent exists. 
  • Drive technical direction across architecture, design, and code reviews, and raise the engineering bar across the incubation. 
  • Mentor senior engineers and lead by influence, not title. 
  • Partner with product, security R&D, SecOps to turn customer problems into architecture, and translate that architecture into decisions leaders can act on. 
  • Establish AI safety, security, governance, and guardrails for agentic systems running in production. 

What you bring 

  • A track record of owning architecture across a large system or multiple teams, with deep experience operating production-quality software. 
  • Hands-on depth in both agentic and LLM systems and probabilistic or ML-driven scoring—graph modeling, calibration, search and optimization, or risk and probability engineering. 
  • Proven zero-to-one at scale: you’ve taken an ambiguous problem to a reliable production system that others depend on. 
  • The judgment to make consequential architecture decisions under uncertainty, and make them defensible to engineers and executives alike. 
  • Command of distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native development, and data or graph systems. 
  • Expert-level Python, and/or Java, Go, or TypeScript. 
  • Technical leadership and mentorship that moves teams through influence. 
  • Applied interest in security problems—attack-path analysis, vulnerability management, identity security, threat intelligence, or detection and response—is strongly preferred. 
  • Experience with AI-assisted development tools and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Windsurf is a plus. 
  • Experience with AI evaluation, safety, governance, or policy guardrails is a plus. 

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including leading the design and delivery of complex production systems. 
  • The primary skills required are Predictive Modeling, Graph ML, Security Analytics, Anomaly Detection, Risk Scoring, LLMs/Agentic AI, and MLOps, which align with advanced machine learning and AI engineering rather than traditional software development.
  • Demonstrated experience as the technical owner or lead for a major system or across teams. 
  • Depth building AI/ML-powered production systems; probabilistic modeling, graph analytics, or calibration and evaluation is a strong plus. 
  • Modern AI experience: LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector search, agentic harness and workflows, model evaluation, or AI observability. 
  • Strong programming experience in Python and/or Java, Go, or a similar language. 
  • Cloud-native technologies, distributed systems, APIs, databases, and scalable architectures. 
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. 
  • Cybersecurity or security-product experience, or familiarity with modern security architectures and operations, is strongly preferred.

Job Description

About the team 

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning. 

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We’re building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability—where an attacker could realistically get in—rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and this role helps define what good looks like. 

The role 

As a Principal ML Engineer, you set the technical vision for exploitability-based security across the portfolio—not just one engine. You define the hardest modeling problems worth solving, set the direction other staff and senior engineers build within, and represent the work to executives, customers, and the broader engineering organization. 

What you’ll own 

  • The technical vision and architecture for exploitability-driven security: where the engine goes next, and the class of problems it should solve beyond any single release. 
  • The hardest unsolved modeling problems—how calibrated attack-path probability holds up across environments, how identity and agent surfaces enter the model, and how ground truth feeds back into it. 
  • The engineering standards and architectural direction that multiple teams build within: scalability, reliability, and the scientific rigor of the scoring. 
  • The build-on strategy across the portfolio: what the engine reuses from existing products, what must be net-new, and why. 

What you’ll do 

  • Set technical direction across multiple teams without direct authority, and turn ambitious ideas into working, enterprise-grade products. 
  • Explore and apply emerging AI to cybersecurity in fundamentally new ways—not simply bolt AI onto existing products. 
  • Represent the team’s technology and innovation with executives, customers, partners, and the broader engineering organization. 
  • Mentor staff and senior engineers, and raise the overall engineering bar through coaching and technical leadership. 
  • Champion AI-native engineering practices, including extensive use of coding agents and autonomous development, testing, evaluation, and operational workflows. 
  • Set the direction for AI safety, security, governance, and guardrails for agentic systems running in production. 

What you bring 

  • Deep expertise in modern AI/ML with a track record of building production AI systems—LLMs, foundation models, agentic architectures, RAG, retrieval, and model evaluation—alongside probabilistic or ML-driven scoring. 
  • The ability to set a compelling technical vision and drive it across teams, then go deep into architecture and code. 
  • A proven record of turning ambitious, ambiguous ideas into products that scale to enterprise workloads. 
  • An innovator’s mindset—challenging conventional approaches and seizing the openings created by rapidly evolving AI. 
  • Command of distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and data or graph systems. 
  • Expert-level Python and modern AI frameworks and infrastructure; experience with Java, Go, or similar languages is valuable. 
  • Executive-level communication: able to articulate a compelling technical vision to engineers, customers, and senior leadership. 
  • Applied depth in security problems—threat detection, vulnerability and exposure management, identity security, risk prioritization, or autonomous remediation—is strongly preferred. 
  • Extensive use of AI-native development tools and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Windsurf across the software development lifecycle. 

Qualifications

  • 15+ years of software engineering experience, including significant technical and engineering leadership responsibility. 
  • The primary skills required are Predictive Modeling, Graph ML, Security Analytics, Anomaly Detection, Risk Scoring, LLMs/Agentic AI, and MLOps, which align with advanced machine learning and AI engineering rather than traditional software development.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and delivering AI/ML-powered products and platforms in production. 
  • Experience leading technical initiatives spanning multiple teams without direct authority. 
  • Demonstrated ability to design systems that scale to enterprise workloads. 
  • Hands-on experience with frontier LLMs, agent frameworks, retrieval and vector technologies, and model evaluation and observability; probabilistic modeling or graph analytics is a strong plus. 
  • Strong backend engineering experience with distributed systems, APIs, microservices, and cloud-native architectures. 
  • Extensive experience using AI-native development tools and coding agents as part of the software development lifecycle. 
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. 
  • Cybersecurity products, or deep familiarity with modern security architectures and security operations, is strongly preferred.

  • A major subsystem end-to-end—the probability core, the exposure graph and entity resolution, or the calibration and validation loop—including its design, delivery, and quality. 
  • The design decisions within your subsystem, and how it interfaces with the rest of the engine. 
  • The metrics that prove your subsystem works—entity-resolution accuracy, calibration quality, or path-ranking precision—owned as first-class targets. 
  • Technical direction for the engineers working in your area. 

What you’ll do 

  • Take a major, ambiguous subsystem from design through production at scale. 
  • Drive design and code reviews in your area, and raise the engineering bar around you. 
  • Mentor engineers and lead a workstream through influence. 
  • Partner with product, security R&D, and SecOps to turn customer problems into subsystem design. 
  • Establish AI safety, security, and guardrails for the agentic parts of your subsystem. 

What you bring 

  • A track record of owning a significant system or subsystem end-to-end in production. 
  • Hands-on depth in agentic and LLM systems and/or probabilistic or ML-driven scoring—graph modeling, calibration, search and optimization. 
  • The primary skills required are Predictive Modeling, Graph ML, Security Analytics, Anomaly Detection, Risk Scoring, LLMs/Agentic AI, and MLOps, which align with advanced machine learning and AI engineering rather than traditional software development.
  • Proven delivery of an ambiguous problem to a reliable production system that others depend on. 
  • The judgment to make sound design decisions under uncertainty within your area. 
  • Command of distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native development, and data or graph systems. 
  • Expert-level Python, and/or Java, Go, or TypeScript. 
  • Technical leadership that moves a workstream through influence. 
  • Applied interest in security problems—attack-path analysis, vulnerability management, identity security, threat intelligence, or detection and response—is preferred. 
  • Experience with AI-assisted development tools and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Windsurf is a plus. 
  • Experience with AI evaluation, safety, governance, or policy guardrails is a plus. 

Qualifications

  • 6+ years of software engineering experience, including leading the design and delivery of complex production components. 
  • The primary skills required are Predictive Modeling, Graph ML, Security Analytics, Anomaly Detection, Risk Scoring, LLMs/Agentic AI, and MLOps. These skills align more closely with advanced machine learning and AI engineering than with traditional software development.

Job Description

Team & Role

This role is part of our Product Design team, which turns a deep understanding of our users and customers into product experiences they love. Our designers bring expertise across design systems, visual design, interaction design, content design, and product design. At ServiceNow, design has an intentional seat at the table, and we partner with engineering and product management from the outset. 

The Design Systems team creates the shared foundations that help ServiceNow teams deliver consistent, accessible, and high-quality product experiences. As Platform and the business units adopt AI-assisted ways of working, designers and front-end engineers need clear standards, practical examples, and reliable ways to check that those standards are being applied. 

We're looking for a Principal Design Technologist to make design-system standards easier to understand, test, and implement. This role translates design-system standards and design files into clear specifications, design-owned coded reference components, validation tools, and implementation guidance. These resources show how an experience should look and behave before Engineering builds and maintains the production implementation. 

Across Design, this principal individual contributor will use deep design and web-development expertise to create coded explorations that demonstrate the intended experience, behavior, and quality of components and AI-enabled interactions. They will mentor product designers who use code to explore and communicate experience concepts and contribute practical insight to the development and adoption of AI-assisted design tools. The role leads through expertise and influence. Product and Engineering retain ownership of product strategy, technical architecture, production code, roadmaps, and delivery. 

What you get to do in this role: 

  • Work with Product Design, Product Management, and Engineering to set the direction for design-system tools and practices that improve quality and adoption across Platform and the business units. 
  • Create and maintain design-owned coded UI reference libraries based on design-system standards and source designs, including Figma where applicable. Use them to demonstrate component states, interactions, responsive behavior, accessibility expectations, and use of design tokens. Engineering owns the production of component libraries and their technical implementation. 
  • Evaluate and create AI-assisted tools that help teams find, apply, and check design-system guidance. Define practical ways to assess whether the tools are accurate, useful, understandable, and aligned with approved standards. 
  • Partner with front-end engineering teams to identify recurring differences between approved designs and delivered experiences. Create design-side review and validation methods that surface issues earlier, and use what teams learn during implementation to improve shared standards, reference components, and guidance. 
  • Lead the adoption of AI tools across Design by evaluating emerging tools, setting responsible working practices, and providing playbooks, demonstrations, workshops, and peer learning that help designers improve quality and work more efficiently. 
  • Mentor and connect product designers who use code to prototype AI experiences. Establish shared working practices, align their explorations with the design system, and turn useful lessons into reusable guidance for the broader design organization. 
  • Collaborate with Product Management and Engineering on the contribution process that enables experts across Design, Engineering, Product, Accessibility, Platform, and the business units to propose, review, and maintain design-system guidance and reference materials. 
  • Partner with Design Enablement and Engineering Operations to help front-end UI engineers use the design system effectively. Contribute design-system onboarding, training, implementation guidance, reference examples, and validation practices, while Engineering Operations leads engineering processes and adoption within the front-end community. 

Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • 12+ years of experience in product design, design systems, design technology, prototyping, or a related discipline within complex, enterprise-scale products. 
  • A portfolio or body of work demonstrating strong systems thinking, interaction and visual craft, and the ability to turn design standards into reusable guidance, reference components, and tools. 
  • Hands-on experience with modern UI frameworks such as Lit and Web Components, with the ability to build coded prototypes and design-owned reference components that clearly demonstrate intended appearance and behavior. 
  • Deep knowledge of design systems, including components, patterns, design tokens, themes, accessibility, responsive behavior, localization, governance, and contribution processes. 
  • Experience using AI to improve design work, such as helping teams find guidance, create and review design-system content, check quality, or automate repeatable tasks. Experience defining appropriate human review and responsible-use practices. 
  • Experience using or extending design tools such as Figma, documentation platforms, component catalogs, analytics, plugins, or automated design-quality and accessibility checks. 
  • Demonstrated success setting direction and influencing senior partners across Design, Product, Engineering, Accessibility, and AI in a complex, distributed organization. 
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, storytelling, critique, and mentoring skills, with a record of helping a broad design organization adopt AI tools, shared standards, and new ways of working. 

Basic Qualifications:  

  • Experience contributing throughout the product development process for web or software products. 
  • Experience in user experience design, product design, design systems, design technology, prototyping, or related field. 
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams across Product, Design, Accessibility, and Engineering.

title: Director, Solution Consulting - CRM Solutions
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started in sunny San Diego, California in 2004 when a visionary engineer, Fred Luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. Fast forward to today — ServiceNow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative AI-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. But this is just the beginning of our journey. Join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone.

Why This Role Matters

You will lead one of  ServiceNow’s fastest-growing markets — and this team will be at the center of that momentum.

You’ll shape how we go to market, how we sell value, and how we build the next generation of Solution Consulting talent.

Job Description

As the Director, North CRM Solution Consulting, you run the day-to-day pre-sales engine for CRM across the Nordics, Benelux, Sweden, and adjacent markets. You lead first-line Solution Consulting managers and  individual contributors, and you are the leader closest to the deals.

You know what each team is working on, what is landing with customers, and what is stalling. Your job is to remove the blockers, keep the team focused and motivated, and make sure Solution Consulting moves in step with its CRM selling peers. This is an execution role at heart: you make the engine go fast.

You report to the AVP, EMEA CRM Solution Consulting, who sets regional strategy and direction.

What you'll do...

Own the number -- deliver CRM NNACV for EMEA North

  • Carry accountability, with your first-line managers, for EMEA North CRM NNACV targets and contribute to the EMEA goal of double-digit ACV growth.
  • Forecast technical win rates and deal-by-deal readiness, and raise risk to the AVP early rather than late.
  • Work with EMEA North CRM sales leaders to focus Solution Consulting time on the opportunities, use cases, and industries where CRM wins fastest.

Know the deals on the ground

  • Maintain a detailed, current view of what each team is working on: active opportunities, technical stage, proof-of-value status, and next steps.
  • Know what is working and what is not, and act on it in the weekly deal and pipeline rhythms rather than in a quarterly review.
  • Join key customer, POV, and escalation discussions where technical credibility or senior air cover is needed.

Remove blockers and keep the team focused

  • Be the first escalation point for anything that slows a deal: environment access, resourcing conflicts, unclear scope, product gaps, or competing demands.
  • Protect the team's time by clearing distractions, cutting low-value requests, and making sure ICs spend their time on the deals that matter most.
  • Make sure every IC knows what good looks like on their deals and has what they need to deliver it.

Lead and develop first-line leaders and ICs

  • Coach first-line managers on deal reviews, technical strategy, and POV execution, and hold them to consistent motions and communication rhythms.
  • Recruit, develop, and retain strong technical talent, and build a bench of ready-now first-line leaders.
  • Give direct, regular feedback to ICs and managers, and address performance issues early.

Keep the team motivated and aligned to selling peers

  • Recognize wins visibly and often, and build a team rhythm that keeps morale and momentum high.
  • Run joint pipeline and deal reviews with CRM sales, value, partner, and product counterparts so Solution Consulting and selling teams operate as one engine.
  • Agree coverage, account plans, and proof strategy with the AEs before they reach the customer.

Drive the shift to POV-centric selling and the FDE model

  • Make working proof-of-value the default way the team earns technical trust, and help ICs move toward the Forward Deployed Engineer model of building alongside customers.
  • Use AI automation tools and standard POV frameworks to speed up demos, environment provisioning, and repeatable assets.

Connect the field to CRM product

  • Channel technical wins, losses, and product gaps from your team to the AVP and CRM product leaders, using specific, deal-level examples.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 6+ years in a leadership role in Solution Consulting or a comparable pre-sales or technical sales function, including managing first-line leaders and individual contributors.
  • Still credible on the deals: you can scope a POV, work through an architecture question, or join a customer call without losing the thread.
  • A consistent record of owning and delivering against ACV / NNACV or equivalent revenue-tied targets in a software or SaaS environment.
  • Experience leading distributed teams across the Nordics, Benelux, Sweden, and adjacent markets and operating effectively across cultures, languages, and time zones.
  • A working understanding of the CRM market and how AI and agentic automation are changing it.
  • Fluency with AI and automation tools and a bias toward using them to simplify how work gets done.
  • Experience moving a team from demo-centric to POV / proof-of-value-centric selling.
  • Clear, direct communication, and the ability to set a standard and hold first-line leaders to it.
  • Good operating judgement: knows when to escalate, when to decide, and when to get out of the way.
  • A talent-focused leader who can recruit, develop, and retain strong technical leaders and ICs.
  • Bachelor's degree in a technical or business field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Expected to travel up to 40% of the time on average, including across the Nordics, Benelux, Sweden, and adjacent markets.

Position overview

A Regional Product Manager (RPM) connects global product strategy to execution in a specific market. Product managers build features and own the core roadmap with engineering teams. At ServiceNow, RPM markets are defined by geography, industry, or customer segment.

In this role, you will own one industry or customer segment in the Americas. You will be the person responsible for how ServiceNow's AI products are positioned, sold, adopted, and improved in that market. This is an individual contributor (IC) role, reporting to the leader of Regional Product Management for the Americas.

Key Responsibilities

Regional strategy and adaptation

  • Translate the global AI product roadmap into a plan for your industry or segment 
  • Tailor use cases, solution packages, and messaging to the operational problems your customers care about most 
  • Account for industry regulations and compliance requirements in how solutions are positioned and deployed 
  • Track AI adoption trends in your market and adjust priorities as they shift 

Go-to-market and sales enablement

  • Partner with sales, marketing, and channel partners to launch AI products into your market 
  • Run discovery on priority deals and shape buying criteria and deal sizing toward AI early in the sales cycle 
  • Build discovery guides, use case catalogs, demo stories, and value stories that sellers can reuse 
  • Make sure AI use cases go live after every win, working with customer success, professional services, and partners on success criteria, go-live dates, and adoption metrics

Commercial strategy and financial targets

  • Own the commercial strategy for your market, including product mix, packaging, and deal structure, to meet revenue and margin targets 
  • Set and own quarterly targets for deals in motion, AI attach, and discovery completed before close 
  • Work with pricing teams on packaging and discount guidance suited to your customers 

Voice of the customer

  • Act as the technical and commercial expert in the field for your market 
  • Gather customer feedback and turn repeated needs into solution requirements for product teams 
  • Test emerging AI ideas with customers and bring the ones with traction to the teams that build new products 
  • Represent ServiceNow with customer executives, at industry events, and in customer advisory sessions 

Competitive intelligence

  • Monitor competitors selling AI into your market, including industry-specific vendors and horizontal AI platforms 
  • Analyze win/loss data to find patterns in why deals are won, lost, or stalled 
  • Equip sales teams with positioning and responses to competitor claims 

Qualifications

To excel as a Regional Product Manager (RPM), you need a unique blend of commercial acumen, cross-cultural leadership, and technical credibility. Because you sit between global development teams and local sales teams, your skillset must balance strategic thinking with ground-level execution.

Commercial and strategic skills

  • You design and run launch plans suited to how your market buys, including the partners, procurement processes, and executives involved 
  • You can set packaging and discount guidance and judge how deal structure affects margin 
  • You turn regulatory and compliance requirements into specific changes in how solutions are built, positioned, and deployed 

Relationship and communication skills

  • You align product teams and field sellers on priorities without direct authority over either 
  • You understand how business and IT leaders in your market make decisions, and you adjust how you communicate with each 
  • You manage expectations with senior product and sales leaders while supporting account teams on high-stakes customer deals 

Analytical and technical skills

  • You use sales data, win/loss results, and market share trends to decide where to focus 
  • You know enterprise AI and platform technology well enough to handle complex objections and train sellers 
  • You turn large volumes of customer feedback into a short, ranked list of requirements product teams can act on 

Experience

  • 10+ years in product management, solution consulting, or go-to-market strategy in enterprise software 
  • Domain depth in at least one industry or customer segment, including its core systems, regulations, and buyers 
  • A track record of influencing enterprise deals through discovery, solution design, or deal structure 
  • Experience taking AI or automation use cases from concept to production at customers 
  • Familiarity with the ServiceNow AI Platform (a plus)

ServiceNow is seeking a customer obsessed Senior Staff Outbound Product Manager to join the Data & Analytics product team responsible for Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB. This is an externally focused role for a product leader who can bring complex enterprise data capabilities to market through clear positioning, product launches, sales enablement, and direct customer engagement.

This role sits at the intersection of data architecture, platform performance, analytics, AI readiness, and customer value. You will help shape how ServiceNow customers understand, adopt, and unlock value from advanced data capabilities, translating deep technical concepts into compelling product narratives, go-to-market strategies, customer-facing content, and field enablement.

Business Context

Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB Professional are strategically important growth areas within ServiceNow’s Data & Analytics portfolio. The business is already significant, with approximately $600M in revenue and a goal to grow to $1.5B by 2029. The opportunity is not simply to sell data as a standalone product, but to build a clear wraparound strategy for how data enhances ServiceNow’s value proposition across workflows, customer outcomes, enterprise AI readiness, and strategic deal pursuits.

The right leader will identify the customer problem, craft the market narrative, and help scale field enablement and growth strategies through one-to-one, one-to-few, and one-to-many motions. This person will partner closely with product, engineering, sales, solution consulting, product marketing, and customer-facing teams to ensure the market understands the value of ServiceNow’s next-generation data platform.

  • Own the outbound product strategy for Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB Professional, translating complex data platform capabilities into clear customer value, differentiated positioning, and compelling market narratives.
  • Define and refine the core messaging, use cases, personas, competitive differentiation, and customer proof points that help technical and executive audiences understand why these products matter.
  • Partner closely with inbound product managers, engineering, product marketing, sales, solution consulting, and customer-facing teams to shape launch strategy, field readiness, growth motions, and adoption plans.
  • Serve as a product evangelist in customer briefings, executive conversations, analyst sessions, webinars, conferences, and strategic deal support, adapting the message for both technical practitioners and business decision-makers.

  • Help establish and track success metrics for outbound initiatives, including launch readiness, seller adoption, customer engagement, pipeline influence, product adoption, and market feedback.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of enterprise software product management, outbound product management, technical product marketing, or go-to-market experience, including ownership of customer-facing launches, positioning, field enablement, and sales plays.
  • Enterprise software experience is required, with a strong preference for candidates who have built, positioned, sold, or taken software products to market for external enterprise customers.
  • Product management or outbound product experience as a builder or seller of software, not solely as an internal IT practitioner, implementation owner, or user of similar technologies.
  • Strong working knowledge of enterprise data and analytics—including data platforms, databases, integrations, cloud infrastructure, analytics, or AI/ML data layers—with the ability to translate these capabilities into differentiated positioning and customer value. Deep engineering or architecture ownership is not required.
  • Strong understanding of how data strategy, integration, data management, databases, and platform capabilities support enterprise AI and workflow transformation.
  • Demonstrated experience engaging external enterprise customers, sellers, and executives through briefings, discovery conversations, launches, field events, or strategic deal support—and using those interactions to sharpen messaging and go-to-market execution.
  • Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to simplify complexity for technical practitioners, business decision-makers, sellers, executives, and customer stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to influence cross-functionally across product, engineering, marketing, sales, solution consulting, customer success, and field teams.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple strategic initiatives in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

Helpful Experience

  • Experience supporting data platform, database, integration/iPaaS, infrastructure, analytics, AI/ML data layer, or enterprise SaaS platform products.
  • Experience delivering demos or supporting technical customer conversations, EBCs, sales engagements, analyst sessions, webinars, conferences, or strategic deal pursuits.

title: Staff Applied Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Tout a commencé sous le soleil de San Diego, en Californie, en 2004, lorsqu’un ingénieur visionnaire, Fred Luddy, a vu le potentiel de transformer notre façon de travailler. Aujourd’hui, ServiceNow se présente comme un leader mondial du marché, apportant une technologie innovante améliorée par l’IA à plus de 8 100 clients, dont 85% des entreprises du Fortune 500®. Notre plateforme intelligente basée sur le nuage connecte de manière transparente les personnes, les systèmes et les processus pour permettre aux organisations de trouver des méthodes de travail plus intelligentes, plus rapides et meilleures. Mais ce n’est que le début de notre voyage. Joignez-vous à nous dans la poursuite de notre objectif de rendre le monde meilleur pour tous.

######

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Dans le rôle de scientifique de recherche appliquée principal(e), vous travaillerez sur des problèmes vaguement définis, pour lesquels aucune méthode éprouvée n’existe encore. ServiceNow AI Research observe le comportement des agents d’IA dans des environnements d’entreprise complexes et à grande échelle. Votre mission consiste à transformer les défis ambigus de ce portrait en orientations concrètes et testables. Vous déciderez quelles questions valent la peine d’être explorées, proposerez les modèles et les techniques pour y répondre, puis construirez, entraînerez et évaluerez vous-même les agents afin de déterminer s’ils fonctionnent.

Vous validerez les nouveaux concepts avant que le reste de l’organisation ne s’y engage. Cela implique de réaliser des prototypes rapidement, de mettre à l’épreuve les hypothèses et de collaborer étroitement avec l’équipe d’ingénierie en déploiement client (Forward Deployed Engineering) pour valider les idées dans des flux de travail réels. Lorsqu’un prototype échoue sur le terrain, c’est vous qui comprendrez pourquoi et qui déterminerez la suite à donner. Vos conclusions orienteront le programme de recherche, la feuille de route produit et les pratiques d’évaluation sur lesquelles l’équipe s’appuie.

Vous définirez aussi la direction technique des projets appliqués dans le cadre du programme plus large de l’équipe, encadrerez les chercheurs et les stagiaires, et représenterez les travaux par des publications, des conférences et des contributions à des projets open source.

#######

As a Staff Applied Research Scientist, you will work on problems that are vaguely defined and have no playbook yet. ServiceNow AI Research sees how AI agents behave in complex enterprise environments at scale, and your job is to turn ambiguous challenges in that picture into concrete, testable directions. You will decide which questions are worth pursuing, propose the models and techniques to answer them, and then build, train, and evaluate the agents yourself to find out whether they work.

You will derisk new concepts before the rest of the organization commits to them. That means prototyping quickly, stress-testing assumptions, and working side by side with the Forward Deployed Engineering team to validate ideas against real customer workflows. When a prototype fails in the field, you will be the one who understands why and what to do next. Your findings will shape the research agenda, the product roadmap, and the evaluation practices that the team relies on.

You will also set technical direction for applied projects within the team's broader agenda, mentor researchers and interns, and represent the work through publications, talks, and open-source contributions.

Qualifications

  • Doctorat en informatique, en apprentissage automatique ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente en recherche ou en application
  • Au moins trois ans d’expérience après le doctorat, incluant du travail sur des systèmes en production ou utilisés par des usagers réels
  • Capacité à décomposer un problème mal défini en ses composantes, à formuler des hypothèses et à concevoir des expériences pour les tester

Armis from ServiceNow, protects the entire attack surface and manages an organization’s cyber risk exposure in real time. Job Description

In this role, you will serve as a trusted technical and business advisor, leading discovery, solution design, product demonstrations, proof-of-value engagements, and customer validation activities. You will work directly with security, identity, infrastructure, IT, risk, and executive stakeholders to connect technical capabilities to measurable business outcomes. 

The ideal candidate has strong cybersecurity knowledge, practical enterprise networking experience, strong communication skills, and a proven ability to support complex enterprise sales cycles. 

Responsibilities 

  • Partner with Sales to lead technical discovery, solution design, and customer validation. 
  • Deliver compelling virtual and in-person technical demonstrations. 
  • Deploy and support proof-of-value and proof-of-concept engagements. 
  • Translate technical capabilities into business outcomes. 
  • Serve as a trusted advisor during evaluations, competitive situations, and executive discussions. 
  • Develop customer-facing documentation, technical summaries, and solution narratives. 
  • Lead technical training sessions based on customer use cases and POV findings. 
  • Support marketing events, conferences, webinars, and speaking engagements. 
  • Collaborate with Product, Enablement, Marketing, Customer Success, and Support teams to share field insights and improve execution. 
  • Travel as required, typically 25–50%, depending on region and business needs. 

Qualifications

Required Qualifications 

  • 5+ years of experience in Solution Consulting, Sales Engineering, Pre-Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or a related technical role. 
  • 5+ years of customer-facing technical, pre-sales, or customer support experience. 
  • Experience supporting complex cybersecurity, SaaS, or enterprise platform sales cycles with enterprise customers. 
  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity concepts, identity and access, governance and risk, and security operations. 
  • Required strong working knowledge of enterprise networking concepts, including routing, switching, VLANs, subnetting, firewalls, DNS, NAT, and network segmentation. 
  • Familiarity with capturing network traffic via SPAN ports, port mirroring, TAPs, packet capture brokers, NetFlow, and network telemetry. 
  • Ability to understand and explain how security platforms integrate with customer network environments to collect data, provide visibility, and support technical validation during demos, POVs, and POCs. 
  • Strong presentation, storytelling, and executive communication skills. 
  • Ability to engage effectively with technical practitioners, business stakeholders, and executive buyers. 
  • Demonstrated track record of contributing to technical wins, deal progression, and successful customer outcomes. 
  • BS degree in Computer Science, MIS, Cybersecurity, or equivalent experience. 

Preferred Experience 

  • Hands-on experience with IAM or IGA solutions 
  • Background in Security Operations or security engineering 
  • Experience with asset discovery across IoT, OT, or IoMT environments 
  • Exposure to vulnerability management or risk-based vulnerability programs 
  • Security, cloud, or relevant technical certifications preferred 
  • Linux or Python scripting experience 

What Success Looks Like 

  • Quickly becomes productive and adds value to active sales pursuits. 
  • Delivery of high-quality demos, POVs, and POCs that advance pipelines. 
  • Build trusted-advisor relationships with customers and Sales partners. 
  • Demonstrates strong technical credibility across complex opportunities. 
  • Connects technical solutions to measurable business outcomes. 
  • Contributes to improved win rates, stronger deal quality, and scalable Solution Consulting execution.

You'll help build the next generation of enterprise language models that bring AI experiences into our customers' day to day work serving more than 9000 enterprise customers worldwide. We're just getting started with our early adopter customers and we need your help building an amazing range of solutions.

What you get to do in this role:

Job Description

The Role

Do you care deeply about secure access at scale? Making sure the right people have the right access, exactly when they need it, without slowing teams down? Join Moveworks and help shape the future of our identity and access strategy.

At Moveworks, we believe great security is an enabler, not a blocker. As a Senior Identity & Access Management Engineer, you’ll be a hands-on technical developer, coding, designing, building, and scaling IAM solutions across cloud infrastructure, SaaS applications, and internal systems. You’ll own the development of IAM initiatives end-to-end, from untangling ambiguous access challenges to architecting secure, automated solutions and driving them into production.

In this role, you’ll develop robust access models across AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, and beyond; reduce privilege sprawl through thoughtful role design; and build strong observability through logging, metrics, and reporting in our SIEM. You’ll modernize access reviews to deliver real security impact with minimal friction, continuously de-risk IAM threats, and partner closely with teams to drive adoption of secure-by-default patterns.

Your work will directly protect Moveworks’ most critical systems while enabling our engineers to move fast, safely, and confidently.


What you get to do in this role:

  • Be the technical developer to drive IAM application development: Code, design, and implement solutions with extensive knowledge in AWS, Azure, Teleport, and Terraform. Enabling robust and reliable solutions to keep our engineering teams active.

  • Drive IAM projects end-to-end: Take ambiguous access problems, understand and have the ability to define requirements, architect solutions, and own the rollout/operationalization (not just the design).

  • Develop with secure access models in mind: Continuously develop role design improvements and access assignment patterns across AWS, Kubernetes, SaaS apps, and internal systems to reduce unnecessary privileges, minimize manual grants, and create scalable “safe baseline” access that covers routine work without daily elevation.

  • Develop on operationalizing logging and metrics: Ensure access changes are observable in our Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tool; build repeatable reporting that surfaces risky access and drift.

  • Run and improve user access reviews (UAR): Develop, execute and design a UAR process & solution that meets compliance requirements while improving real security signal—minimizing approver burden through scoping, automation, and clear decision support.

  • Develop technology to continuously de-risk: Identify high-risk permissions and misuse paths, propose appropriate controls and mitigations, drive adoption with partner teams, and develop solutions to continuously de-risk.

  • Operate with strong security judgment and high signal: Reliably distinguish meaningful IAM risk from noise, gather context efficiently, and escalate with crisp rationale and actionable mitigations.

  • Document and standardize the paved road: Write lightweight procedures, runbooks, and automation so access decisions are consistent, scalable, and not dependent on tribal knowledge.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience: 5+ years of experience developing and maintaining IAM products/tools.

  • Automation-first mindset: Experience writing production-ready scalable software, Infrastructure as Code, and using AI coding tools to build reliable automation.

  • IAM Expertise: Strong grasp of IAM best practices, techniques, and common failure modes (e.g., least privilege, privilege escalation paths, separation of duties, breakglass, auditability). Ability to spot dangerous permissions and identify suitable mitigations and controls.

  • Educational Background: BS+ in computer science or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

  • US Citizenship preferred

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the role

Health Log Analytics (HLA) ingests, stores, and analyzes the logs that power ServiceNow's AIOps suite. We want it to be the data backbone teams trust to find problems early and fix them fast.

HLA is a data platform for operational logs at high volume, built for ServiceNow’s large enterprise customers. The work spans the full data path: collection and ingestion, routing and enrichment, durable storage and retention, and fast, cost-aware query. Our ingest builds on OpenTelemetry, and we have our own Rust-based log storage. As data volume, customer needs, and AI-driven use cases grow, we need the platform to get more reliable, more efficient, and more useful.

We're looking for a senior technical leader to help set where HLA goes next. You'll work side by side with engineering and product leadership on the roadmap. You'll bring a clear point of view and show it with a prototype, not just a slide.

You'll set the technical bar for experienced engineers. You'll do it by being a great teammate, not the loudest person in the room.

What you'll do

  • Help shape the HLA roadmap with engineering, product, and leadership. Bring both vision and a reality check.
  • Work directly with customers to make sure HLA keeps delivering value as their needs change. Turn their feedback into clear, actionable input for product and the roadmap.
  • Set architecture direction across ingest, storage, and query, and across teams you don't own.
  • Write down your point of view, then build a prototype that helps others see it and get behind it.
  • Say no, with reasons. That includes AI ideas with no evidence behind them, and timelines or designs that don't fit today's constraints. Know when to push past those constraints, too.
  • Lead deep design reviews that raise the bar and leave people feeling sharper, not smaller.
  • Define the reliability and efficiency bar for the HLA data path: completeness, durability, latency, availability, tenant isolation, and unit cost.
  • Lead the technical approach to hard transitions, such as storage migrations, schema changes, replay, and upgrades with little or no downtime.
  • Set clear architectural boundaries and contracts for the teams building collection, ingest, storage, anomaly detection, query, and AIOps experiences.
  • Show how we build with AI. Weigh ideas against customer value, data quality, reliability, and cost. Run small experiments to help us decide what to scale.
  • Set the example on quality, on-call, and learning from incidents.
  • Mentor senior engineers and tech leads. Help grow the next technical leaders.
  • Work as a real partner to engineering and product leadership. Learn in the open.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have  

  • Experience in leveraging or critical thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision making, or problem solving. This includes using AI powered tools, automated workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or reasoning about AI’s impact on how infrastructure is built and run.
  • 12+ years building and operating production distributed systems, with substantial ownership of large-scale data or platform systems. Equivalent depth shown through sustained technical leadership counts too.
  • Broad grounding across data ingestion, storage and query, and AI on top of data. Deep expertise in at least one.
  • Experience with ingest tools like Kafka, Pulsar, or Kinesis, and with columnar stores, time-series databases, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, or object-storage designs
  • A record of changing the direction of teams you didn't own, through credibility and clear thinking
  • Evidence-based judgment on AI. You know where it belongs and where it doesn’t, and you’ve built safeguards for correctness, safety, and cost. You’ve shipped with it, or you’re a strong proponent with a clear point of view.
  • Good judgment on tradeoffs: consistency, latency, cost, and operational burden
  • Comfort with Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure at scale
  • Fluency in at least one of Go, Java, Scala, Rust, or Python. You prototype and review deeply, and you write code when it counts.
  • Clear communication. You can explain a tricky design to a new hire or a VP and have both of them get it.

Nice to Have: 

  • A background in observability, log analytics, OpenTelemetry or AIOps
  • Experience at an AI-native company, or building agents and LLM-based features
  • Experience with multitenant SaaS and per-tenant isolation

Who you are

  • Humble, smart, and you care about people
  • You have experience working remotely and leading remote teams
  • You make the people around you better, and you share the work and the credit
  • You're comfortable when the problem isn't fully defined, and you help define it
  • You turn small, messy things into big, solid ones
  • You care about the people who run what you build

Why join us

You'll work on real scale problems with real customers. You'll have room to shape the architecture and the direction of a product that matters. And you'll join a team that values clear thinking, honest feedback, and shipping.
