Job Description

ServiceNow is seeking a Sr Staff Solution Architect to lead the design and delivery of scalable, intelligent, and high-impact solutions across the Connected Customer Experience portfolio. This is a senior-level, hands-on architecture role focused on enabling seamless digital workflows, integrating platform capabilities with AI/ML and data-driven insights, and ensuring technical excellence across customer-facing applications.

You will work at the intersection of product, engineering, platform, data, and AI teams to architect solutions that enhance user experience, deliver personalized customer journeys, and drive measurable business outcomes. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in enterprise SaaS architecture, CRM systems, solution design, AI/ML integration, and data platform engineering within Digital Technology (DT) environments.

Key Responsibilities

Solution Architecture & Design

  • Architect scalable, secure, and compliant end-to-end solutions integrating platform capabilities with intelligent data-driven features across customer experience applications.
  • Define architecture patterns for workflows, integrations, platform extensions, and API-driven services that extend ServiceNow capabilities while ensuring alignment with security and platform standards.
  • Lead evolution of architectural standards, evaluate tools and frameworks, and partner with product and engineering leaders to translate business requirements into technical designs.

AI/ML & Data Platform

  • Architect AI/ML capabilities for personalization, recommendations, semantic search, and conversational AI with service layers that enable easy consumption by product teams.
  • Design unified data architecture bringing together customer signals across touchpoints, including data lakes, warehouses, real-time pipelines, and analytical products.
  • Establish governance frameworks for data quality, privacy, security, and compliance (GDPR, CCPA) while ensuring data readiness and pipeline integration.
  • Define architecture for model observability, performance monitoring, and continuous learning feedback loops.

Technical Strategy & Leadership

  • Define multi-year architectural roadmaps and lead architectural reviews, governance processes, and critical modeling decisions across product verticals.
  • Translate complex designs into accessible, secure services ensuring observability, performance, and operational excellence while mentoring architects and senior engineers.
  • Provide thought leadership on emerging technologies and foster a culture of technical excellence.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 15+ years in enterprise software architecture, solution design, or technical leadership with significant CRM and enterprise SaaS platform experience.
  • Proven track record designing production-grade solutions across customer service, digital workflows, CRM, or customer experience platforms.
  • Deep expertise in microservices, event-driven architectures, API-first design, cloud-native technologies, and security best practices.
  • Strong understanding of AI/ML systems with hands-on experience in personalization, NLP/NLU, semantic search, or conversational AI.
  • Experience with data platform architecture including data modeling, ETL/ELT pipelines, streaming, data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), and data governance.
  • Familiarity with ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Hugging Face), MLOps tools, and data processing tools (Spark, dbt, Airflow).
  • Excellent communication skills with ability to influence stakeholders across cross-functional, matrixed global organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ServiceNow platform and extending its capabilities through custom applications or intelligent services.
  • Deep understanding of CRM platforms (Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, ServiceNow CSM) and their integration with customer experience ecosystems.
  • Background in customer journey orchestration, personalized digital experiences, or recommendation engines in large-scale SaaS environments.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM integration, prompt engineering, RAG, and vector databases for GenAI applications.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, DevOps practices, and experience in global, matrixed organizations.

What We Offer

  • A high-impact role shaping customer experience architecture within one of the world's leading enterprise platforms.
  • The opportunity to define architectural strategies for mission-critical applications serving millions of users.
  • A collaborative, innovation-focused culture with organizational influence and visibility to senior leadership.

Job Description

About the Role 

As a Sr Customer Success Manager, you sit at the crossroads of innovation, enterprise scale, and real-world impact. With Moveworks and ServiceNow now operating as one company, this role plays a pivotal part in delivering on a shared vision: bringing the front door of AI to every employee while strengthening enterprise workflows through the Moveworks AI Assistant, powered by the ServiceNow platform. 

You will guide customers through transformational journeys, helping them realize measurable business outcomes by pairing intelligent automation with deeply integrated enterprise workflows. You are both strategist and operator: a trusted advisor to executives, an advocate for the customer internally, and a driver of adoption, value, and long-term partnership. 

Who We Are 

Moveworks, now part of ServiceNow, is redefining how work gets done. Together, we combine Moveworks’ industry-leading AI Assistant with ServiceNow’s world-class workflow platform to deliver instant, intelligent support across IT, HR, Finance, and beyond. 

Our shared mission is simple and ambitious: make work better for people. We do this by resolving employee needs instantly, automating complex workflows, and enabling enterprises to operate faster, smarter, and at scale. 

What You’ll Do 

  • Own and grow a portfolio of 25 or more mid market & enterprise customers, guiding them from go live through long-term value realization 
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to executive sponsors, aligning AI-driven solutions to strategic business outcomes 
  • Drive adoption, engagement, and expansion of the Moveworks AI Assistant across ServiceNow workflows 
  • Translate customer business needs into actionable solutions, influencing roadmap and product evolution 
  • Identify, quantify, and track customer success metrics tied to efficiency, cost savings, and employee experience 
  • Proactively manage risks, expectations, and change, ensuring customers successfully navigate complex environments 
  • Act as the voice of the customer internally, sharing insights, feedback, and success stories 
  • Support renewal and expansion motions by demonstrating ongoing value and business impact 

Qualifications

What You Bring

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Implementation, or Consulting within SaaS 
  • Experience supporting medium to large enterprise customers and navigating complex stakeholder environments 
  • Strong ability to explain technical and AI-driven solutions in clear, business-oriented terms 
  • Familiarity with workflow platforms, ITSM, HR systems, or enterprise automation (ServiceNow experience a plus) 
  • Proven ability to build executive relationships and influence outcomes at multiple levels 
  • Process-oriented mindset with strong problem-solving and change management skills 
  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving, evolving product environments 
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience 
  • Willingness to travel approximately 10–25% 

Why This Role Matters 

This is not a traditional Customer Success role. You are helping define how AI shows up in everyday work, turning complexity into clarity for millions of employees. descriptionHtml:

Job Description

As a Sales Coach, you will work one on one with sellers to lift pipeline generation, deal quality, and forecast accuracy. This is a hands-on field coaching role. You will spend most of your week with sellers and in live deal work, and the rest building the programs that scale what works. You report to the manager of the department and partner closely with frontline sales managers, enablement, product marketing, and the teams integrating newly acquired sellers.

What you get to do in this role:

Coach sellers one on one - This is the center of the role. You will spend most of your week with individual sellers, working on whatever stands between them and their number.

● Run a recurring one-on-one coaching cadence with each assigned seller against a written individual development plan

● Coach the full seller motion—prospecting and outbound rigor, territory and account management, deal management and qualification, executive presence, time and calendar management, CRM accuracy and forecast hygiene, and personal change management through reorgs and portfolio shifts

● Facilitate role plays and certification checkpoints across discovery, executive conversations, pricing, objection handling, and competitive positioning, so mastery is demonstrated rather than assumed

● Observe live customer calls and give same-day feedback that names the specific behavior to change

Build coaching programs with your manager

● Partner with your manager to design programs that answer real business needs—segment ramp paths, focused skill sprints, manager coaching enablement, and remediation tracks

● Build segment-appropriate variants where Enterprise and Commercial need different treatment of the same skill—multi-stakeholder pursuit strategy and executive alignment on one side, call volume, cycle discipline, and portfolio juggling on the other

● Design coaching that scales across a large Commercial population without losing the personal quality that makes coaching work

● Contribute reusable assets back to the global library: playbooks, call frameworks, role play scenarios, and certification rubrics

● Pilot, measure, and retire—keep what moves the number and cut what does not

Support large-scale training events

● Help design and deliver org-wide moments: sales kickoff, bootcamps, mid-year kickoffs, product launch enablement, and field readiness days

● Own assigned tracks end to end—content, facilitators, breakout design, certification, and the reinforcement plan that follows

● Build the follow-through so event content shows up in seller behavior 30 and 60 days later

Document and report progress

● Build and maintain the documentation layer that makes coaching visible and auditable—rep scorecards, skill matrices, certification records, development plans, and progress over time

● Report coaching impact to sales and enablement leadership on a set cadence, tied to business results rather than activity counts

● Keep records consistent enough that another coach could pick up any rep and know exactly where they stand

Shorten time to productivity for new hires, transfers, and acquired teams

● Own the coaching side of ramp for new hires, internal transfers, and sellers joining through acquisition, with an explicit goal of moving time to productivity from roughly six months to three

● Build and run acquisition-specific enablement: cross-portfolio positioning, joint account mapping, tooling and process conversion, and the cultural onboarding that makes acquired sellers feel like part of the team quickly

● Track ramp milestones by cohort and flag an at-risk ramp early enough to fix it

● Give hiring managers a clear read on where each new seller stands and what they need next

Validate readiness on new products, releases, and acquisitions

● Assess whether sellers are genuinely equipped to sell new products, new releases, and newly acquired portfolios—measured through certification, call review, and pipeline evidence, not attendance

● Report readiness gaps to product, marketing, and enablement partners with a recommended fix and a date

● Re-test after remediation and close the loop

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

● Seven or more years in enterprise or commercial software sales, sales management, or sales coaching and enablement

● Direct experience with both a large-deal Enterprise motion and a higher-velocity Commercial or mid-market motion, and a clear point of view on how coaching differs between them

● A track record of coaching adults to behavior change—specific sellers or teams who improved on a measurable metric because of your work

● Fluency in at least one recognized sales methodology, such as MEDDICC, Challenger, Strategic Selling, or Command of the Message, and the ability to coach to it rather than just describe it

● Strong CRM discipline—you can inspect a pipeline and tell the difference between a data problem and a deal problem

● Comfort with the enablement stack: CRM, conversation intelligence, sales content management, and a learning management system

● Credibility with senior sellers and frontline managers—this role carries influence, not authority

● Excellent facilitation and written communication skills, and the judgment to know when to teach and when to ask

Nice to Have:

● Prior quota-carrying experience at both Enterprise and Commercial

● Experience coaching across a multi-product or platform portfolio

● Formal coaching certification, such as ICF or equivalent

● Experience integrating an acquired sales team

Job Description

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO) 

The ServiceNow Security Organization (SSO) delivers world-class, innovative security solutions to reduce risk and protect the company and our customers. We enable our customers to migrate their most sensitive data and workloads to the cloud, accelerating our business so that we are the most trusted SaaS provider. We create an environment where our employees are proud to work and can make a positive impact

ServiceNow seeks a senior staff-level product security engineer to serve as a senior technical authority within the Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT). PSIRT is ServiceNow's awareness, response, and investigation capability for post-release vulnerabilities in ServiceNow-developed products and service offerings.

This role is for a recognized expert who can operate independently and as part of a team on the most significant security issues facing the platform—vulnerabilities that require evaluating intangibles. You will lead deep-dive investigations, coordinate resolution across engineering, product, and release teams, and demonstrate calm, decisive leadership during significant security events.

This is a role for someone who already understands product development cycles and the engineering and product relationships that drive them—and will use that fluency to lead fixes to completion under incident pressure. You will help shape how ServiceNow responds to product security vulnerabilities at scale and the technical rigor of the entire response capability.

The coverage provided by this role is:

  • Sunday-Monday: 18:00 - 02:00 UTC
  • Monday-Tuesday: 18:00 - 02:00 UTC
  • Tuesday-Wednesday: 18:00 - 02:00 UTC
  • Friday-Saturday: 19:00 - 02:00 UTC
  • Saturday-Sunday: 17:00 - 02:00 UTC

Due to the nature of incident response and needs of the business, coverage may change. Additional coverage outside of stated hours may be required in response to significant incidents.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Demonstrate technical and organizational leadership during these events—bringing structure and clear decision-making under pressure.
  • Partner with incident commanders, business information security leadership, engineering, and customer-facing teams to maintain clear ownership, workstream prioritization, and hand-offs during these events.

Reduce Exposure Window

  • Drive coordinated response across affected releases, balancing risk and remediation feasibility.
  • Leverage an understanding of product development cycles and engineering/product partnerships to move fixes through the release pipeline without stalling on organizational boundaries.

Drive the CVE & Coordinated Disclosure Process

  • Represent PSIRT's technical position in multi-party coordinated disclosures and researcher engagements.

Pursue After-Action Outcomes & Continuous Improvement

  • Author postmortems and drive lessons learned to closure following product security incidents.
  • Participate in retrospectives following significant product security events, translating findings into concrete process and technical improvements.
  • Contribute to partner teams tracking product security risk themes and trends across the portfolio.
  • Contribute to SDLC improvement areas, feeding incident learnings upstream into secure development practices.

Qualifications

title: Sr. Staff Product Manager, AI-Native IT Service Management
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team 

Service Operations is where enterprises find out whether their technology actually works. An outage starts, someone gets paged, a bridge call spins up, and the first twenty minutes go to working out what broke rather than fixing it. 

Our team owns the products that close that gap: incident and major incident, problem and root cause, change, on-call, and Notify. The people using them go well beyond the service desk, from application, platform, infrastructure, and network teams to DevOps and SRE groups who get alerted around the clock and the major incident commanders pulling everyone onto one call. Thousands of the largest IT organizations run their operations on these products. We are rebuilding them AI-native, not AI-assisted, with agents that triage, correlate, and resolve, and with people moving from doing the work to directing it. Our goal is Zero Service Outage. 

About the role 

You will own a piece of that portfolio outright: what good looks like for it, who it is for, and whether we are honestly there yet. Zero Service Outage is the goal, and the work is making it true for the customers who run their operations on these products every day. 

The interesting part of this job is not the model. It is the environment it runs in. Service operations data is the messiest data in the enterprise: half-populated CMDBs, incident descriptions written in a hurry at 2am, alert noise from a dozen monitoring tools, and naming conventions that differ by region. An agent that triages perfectly against a clean eval set can behave very differently against a real customer’s incident stream, for reasons that have nothing to do with reasoning ability. Understanding why, and designing for it, is the job. 

We also carry an installed base. Customers run today’s experience in production, and moving them onto an AI-native one is not a UI refresh. It is a change to how their IT team works, who approves what, and what an operator trusts an agent to do unsupervised. You will be making calls about what we carry forward, what we leave behind, and what we have to earn the right to automate. 

How we work is changing as fast as what we build. Prototype instead of describing the idea. Put a working demo in front of people instead of a slide about a demo. Draft the spec, stand up a rough eval harness, pull your own data. ServiceNow invests in state-of-the-art tooling and expects you to use it. Product managers are better positioned than anyone to lead that shift, and part of this role is pulling the team around you into it. 

What you get to do in this role 

  • Own an AI-native ITSM product end to end, from the customer problem through launch criteria to how it performs in production. 

  • Set product strategy for the Service Operations portfolio that supports ServiceNow’s growth toward $10B+ in revenue. 

  • Build, not just specify. Prototype the interaction, stand up the eval harness, and get into the agent execution logs to understand what happened on the runs that failed. 

  • Define what good means for an autonomous agent in an operational context where the cost of a wrong action is a second outage. Hold the line on it with engineering and have the honest conversation about what we can defensibly promise. 

  • Work with design partners across the teams that run on this: service desk, application and infrastructure support, DevOps and SRE, and major incident command. Build in their environment against their real incidents, changes, and RCAs, then turn what you learn into something that generalizes to the next thousand customers. 

  • Own your outcome metrics, such as time to resolve, change failure rate, and repeat incidents, in partnership with Customer Success, and make sure the instrumentation exists to show whether what you shipped moved them. 

  • Align with peer product managers so the team is working on the right things at the right time and guide multiple teams through ambiguous product development without losing sight of the unified vision. 

  • Write the strategy, the specs, and the analysis yourself. 

  • Coach other product managers. This is a senior role on a small team, and how you raise the people around you counts as much as what you ship. 

Qualifications

Qualifications 

  • 12+ years of software product management experience, including a track record of shipping complex enterprise products that customers love and that drive meaningful business outcomes. 

  • Have owned an AI-native product end to end and been the person accountable for its quality bar. The ownership is what matters, not the years. 

  • Know what enterprise-grade means for AI: the quality bar, the guardrails, the telemetry, and the work of earning a customer’s trust before they hand an agent real authority. 

  • Have working knowledge of IT service operations: how incidents, changes, and on-call actually run, and why operations teams are slow to trust automation. You know these domains well enough to identify what should change fundamentally, not just incrementally. 

  • Comfortable with platform concepts such as workflow orchestration, workspace design, Flow Designer, and extensibility patterns. You can engage in architecture discussions and make informed trade-offs. 

  • Experience working with large enterprises that have complex customizations, compliance requirements, and high expectations. 

  • Experience defining and capturing product requirements, from customer insights and market analysis to detailed user stories and product roadmaps that align stakeholders and guide execution. 

  • Deep curiosity about customer needs and a track record of building authentic customer relationships. 

  • Ability to drive solution development through systems thinking and to serve as a product lead and mentor for more junior team members. 

  • Experience integrating AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving, whether through AI-powered tools, workflow automation, or analysis of AI-driven insights. 

Preferred qualifications 

  • Depth in IT service operations: incident and major incident, change, problem and RCA, CMDB, on-call, or AIOps. You have been on the bridge call, or close enough to know how the first thirty minutes go. 

  • Agent evaluation: eval set design, LLM-as-judge, and closing the gap between offline results and production behavior. 

  • Hands-on prototyping and analysis. You work in the tooling, the data, and the logs rather than describing them. 

  • Zero-to-one experience, where the users, the quality bar, and the economics all had to be worked out at once. 

  • Experience migrating a large installed base onto a materially different experience. 

  • AI-native working habits that are already default, and evidence that you have changed how a team around you works. 

  • Familiarity with other enterprise workflow platforms such as Salesforce, Jira Service Management, Freshworks, and BMC.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem  across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources  providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance. 

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents.  For engineers joining Veza today, this means the scale and resources of an enterprise platform company, with the product velocity and mission-driven focus of a security innovator at a pivotal moment in the industry.

descriptionHtml:

Job Description

We are hiring across multiple engineering levels. Final level alignment is determined by experience, technical expertise, demonstrated impact, and interview performance. 

Join the Compute Engineering organization, which builds the scheduling, capacity, and performance systems that run our platform across private and public cloud. 

 What you get to do in this role:

  • Design and evolve the compute scheduler and resource-management systems, including placement, prioritization, preemption, and fairness across workloads. 
  • Build capacity models and forecasts across private and public cloud, and turn them into reservation and placement decisions. 
  • Establish performance and scale testing: benchmarks, load tests, regression detection, and SLOs for scheduling latency and throughput. 
  • Apply AI and ML to forecasting, anomaly detection, and placement optimization where they outperform simpler approaches. 
  • Write and maintain declarative, software-defined infrastructure at scale, with build systems, web services, and automation that are specified, documented, and testable. 
  • Research and adopt open-source and commercial tools and methods that improve compute efficiency and reliability. 
  • Partner with networking, orchestration, SRE, and FinOps teams on cross-team designs and cost trade-offs. 
  • Guide complex technical decisions and design reviews. Challenge assumptions with data, surface architectural risks early, and balance shipping speed with long-term durability. 
  • Own production reliability and incident response for compute systems, and lead post-incident improvements. 
  • Mentor architects and senior engineers and build the next layer of technical leadership. 

Level expectations 

  • Senior Staff : Leads the design and delivery of a major component of the compute platform. Drives quality within a team and mentors engineers. 
  • Principal : Sets technical direction across multiple teams or a major compute area. Shapes architecture, mentors senior engineers and architects, and influences decisions across geographies. 

Qualifications

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 12+ years of related experience in software engineering, cloud, or infrastructure automation with a Bachelor's degree; or 8+ years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 5+ years of experience; or equivalent experience. 
  • Deep experience designing multi-tenant, cloud-native SaaS at enterprise scale, including distributed systems, large-scale data systems, APIs, and microservices. 
  • Experience designing or operating large-scale schedulers or resource managers, such as Kubernetes, Slurm, or internal equivalents. 
  • Strong programming skills in Go, Python, or Java, with experience in related languages. 
  • Experience with capacity planning, performance engineering, or load testing at scale. 
  • Hands-on experience applying ML in production, including models, feature pipelines, or ML platforms. Using AI tools alone is not enough. 
  • Experience with infrastructure as code and configuration management, such as Terraform and Ansible. 
  • Comfortable with virtualization and cloud infrastructure across private and public clouds, such as Azure, AWS, GCP. 
  • Working understanding of IP networking, block and file storage, and load balancers. 
  • Experience integrating AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem solving. 
  • Works independently across interconnected systems and investigates root causes without waiting for direction. 
  • Influences without direct authority across multiple teams and geographies (US, EU, India). 
  • Communicates clearly with senior leaders, customers, and engineers, and articulates a compelling technical vision. 
  • Has a learning mindset and is motivated to build new skills and bring real improvement to internal and external customers. 
  • Has integrity and honesty, and upholds ServiceNow's values. 

Preferred 

  • Experience with ML-driven scheduling, forecasting, or capacity optimization. 
  • Working knowledge of internet protocols such as DNS, NTP, and HTTP. 
  • Experience with release management and large-scale server infrastructure.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Global Partnerships & Channels (GPC) 

At ServiceNow, we put AI to work for people. Our AI platform connects any AI, any data, and any workflow to help organizations work smarter, move faster, and reinvent how business gets done. Global Partnerships & Channels extends that impact through a worldwide ecosystem of strategic, technology, cloud, service, and solution partners. 

Role Overview 

The Executive Administrative Assistant (EAA) to the GPC Leader is a highly trusted administrative partner responsible for maximizing the effectiveness, productivity, and operating capacity of a global executive leading one of ServiceNow’s most strategic and fast-moving organizations. 

This is an AI-forward executive support role requiring demonstrated proficiency with AI-enabled Executive Assistant (AI EA) tools and platforms, in addition to broader AI and automation capabilities. The successful candidate already uses AI EA tools as an integrated part of how they manage executive calendars, scheduling, meeting preparation, follow-up, travel, communications, task management, and executive-office workflows. 

We are looking for someone who can show how they have personally used AI EA technology to improve the way an executive office operates—not simply someone who is familiar with AI, uses a general-purpose AI assistant, or is interested in learning these tools. 

The GPC Leader operates at an exceptionally fast pace across a global ecosystem of ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, industry leaders, and employees. Priorities can shift rapidly and often require immediate action. The EAA must operate with exceptional agility, adaptability, flexibility, judgment, and precision while maintaining accuracy and continuity across a constantly changing executive agenda. 

This role goes well beyond traditional calendar administration. The EAA is a force multiplier for the executive, combining exceptional executive support capabilities with AI EA technology, automation, and modern productivity practices to anticipate needs, eliminate friction, create operating leverage, and continually improve how work gets done. 

What You’ll Do 

AI EA Tools, Automation & Executive Productivity 

  • Demonstrate advanced, hands-on proficiency using AI-enabled Executive Assistant tools and platforms specifically designed to support executive administration and executive-office workflows. 

  • Integrate AI EA tools into daily work to improve complex scheduling, calendar optimization, meeting preparation, briefing and context development, action and commitment tracking, follow-up, travel coordination, communications, and executive workflow management. 

  • Use AI EA capabilities to anticipate conflicts, identify scheduling and workflow dependencies, surface outstanding actions, organize executive priorities, and reduce administrative friction. 

  • Determine which work is best performed through specialized AI EA tools, broader AI platforms, workflow automation, or direct human judgment and intervention. 

  • Build and continually improve an AI-enabled administrative operating model that increases executive capacity while maintaining exceptional accuracy, discretion, responsiveness, and stakeholder experience. 

  • Identify repetitive or inefficient administrative processes and redesign them using AI EA capabilities, automation, integrations, templates, and other productivity technologies. 

  • Apply appropriate quality controls to AI-supported work, independently validating outputs and maintaining accountability for accuracy, confidentiality, and final execution. 

  • Remain current on emerging AI EA technologies and proactively evaluate and adopt capabilities that can measurably improve executive and administrative productivity. 

Executive Calendar, Time & Priority Management 

  • Own a highly complex, dynamic global executive calendar involving C-suite leaders, senior internal executives, customers, strategic partners, industry leaders, and employees. 

  • Manage the calendar as a strategic business tool, ensuring executive time is aligned to the highest-value business, customer, partner, talent, and leadership priorities. 

  • Make rapid, thoughtful decisions when priorities change, understanding what can move, what cannot, who needs to be informed, and what downstream implications must be addressed. 

  • Anticipate conflicts, preparation requirements, decision points, travel implications, and follow-up needs before they become issues. 

  • Reprioritize quickly and confidently in an environment where the executive’s schedule may change multiple times in a day. 

  • Protect focus time while preserving the flexibility required of a highly visible global leader. 

Internal & External Executive Engagements 

  • Orchestrate internal and external executive engagements from initial request through preparation, execution, and follow-up. 

  • Coordinate engagements with ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, industry leaders, external organizations, and other high-priority stakeholders. 

  • Ensure the executive enters critical engagements with the right context, objectives, participants, materials, logistics, and preparation. 

  • Maintain visibility to commitments and follow-up resulting from executive engagements and ensure actions move forward quickly. 

  • Coordinate across executive offices and external organizations to create a highly professional, responsive, and seamless stakeholder experience. 

  • Represent the GPC Leader with discretion, confidence, sound judgment, and strong executive presence. 

GPC Leadership & Operating Rhythm 

  • Enable the operating rhythm of the GPC leadership team, including leadership meetings, business reviews, planning sessions, executive offsites, talent discussions, company events, and key partner engagements. 

  • Partner closely with the Chief of Staff to translate business priorities into an effective executive cadence and use of the leader’s time. 

  • Maintain a working understanding of GPC priorities, key decisions, leadership commitments, and upcoming milestones so administrative decisions can be made with appropriate business context. 

  • Connect meetings, decisions, commitments, and follow-up rather than treating individual calendar events as isolated activities. 

  • Anticipate what the leader and leadership team will need next and initiate action without waiting for direction. 

Cross-Functional Executive Office Partnership 

  • Work closely with the Chief of Staff, HR Business Partner, Executive Communications, Finance, Strategy, and other key functions to coordinate and sequence executive priorities. 

  • Serve as a highly effective connector across teams, ensuring information, decisions, requests, and follow-up move at the pace required by the business. 

  • Coordinate executive communications, leadership forums, company events, talent engagements, organizational activities, and external commitments. 

  • Establish strong working relationships with executive assistants across ServiceNow and with the offices of customers, partners, and other external executives. 

Global Travel & Executive Logistics 

  • Manage complex domestic and international travel, including rapidly changing itineraries, executive meetings, partner/customer engagements, events, and associated logistics. 

  • Anticipate travel dependencies and resolve issues quickly, often with limited notice and across multiple time zones. 

  • Integrate travel, meetings, preparation, and executive priorities into a cohesive plan rather than managing each independently. 

  • Remain highly responsive when critical executive needs or schedule changes require flexibility outside traditional working hours. 

Qualifications

What You Bring 

  • Certification in Certified Administrative Professional (CAP) or equivalent administrative credential preferred. 

  • 7+ years of progressive experience supporting senior executives, preferably at the SVP, EVP, or C-suite level in a global technology, high-growth, or similarly fast-paced environment. 

  • Demonstrated proficiency with AI-enabled Executive Assistant (AI EA) tools and platforms. This is a core requirement of the role—not simply general familiarity or fluency with AI. 

  • Proven experience personally incorporating AI EA tools into executive administrative workflows such as complex calendar and scheduling management, meeting preparation, executive briefing, action tracking, follow-up, travel, communications, and productivity management. 

  • Ability to provide specific examples of AI EA tools used, the executive-administration problems addressed, how the tools were incorporated into daily workflows, and the resulting improvements in speed, efficiency, accuracy, or executive capacity. 

  • Broader proficiency with generative AI, workflow automation, and productivity technologies, with the ability to combine these capabilities with specialized AI EA tools. 

  • Demonstrated success supporting a global executive operating at exceptional speed, with complex stakeholder demands and priorities that can change rapidly. 

  • Exceptional agility, adaptability, and flexibility, including the ability to reprioritize and execute quickly without sacrificing accuracy. 

  • Exceptional attention to detail and a demonstrated record of accuracy in high-volume, high-velocity executive environments. 

  • Advanced ability to manage highly complex global calendars and make independent prioritization decisions with limited direction. 

  • A productivity and continuous-improvement mindset: instinctively identifies opportunities to simplify, automate, standardize, eliminate unnecessary work, and improve how the executive office operates. 

  • Exceptional judgment, discretion, executive presence, and ability to manage highly sensitive and confidential information. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and confidence engaging with senior internal executives, customers, partners, and external stakeholders. 

  • A highly anticipatory working style—the ability to recognize what is needed, understand implications, and act before being asked. 

  • Ability to remain composed and highly effective amid ambiguity, urgency, last-minute change, and competing demands. 

What Success Looks Like 

  • The GPC Leader has more capacity because of this partnership. Executive time is focused on the highest-value priorities, administrative friction is reduced, and the executive office operates at extraordinary speed without sacrificing accuracy or stakeholder experience. 

  • AI EA technology is embedded in the day-to-day operation of the executive office. Specialized AI EA tools, broader AI capabilities, and automation are intentionally applied to reduce administrative burden, accelerate execution, improve accuracy, strengthen follow-through, and increase executive capacity. 

  • Internal and external executive engagements are exceptionally well orchestrated. The leader has the right context at the right time; stakeholders receive timely, professional engagement; commitments do not get lost; and changes are absorbed without unnecessary disruption. 

  • The EAA is a trusted extension of the GPC Leader—able to keep pace, anticipate what is coming, adapt immediately when circumstances change, and continually increase the productivity of the executive and broader leadership team. 

Why This Role Matters 

Global Partnerships & Channels is central to how ServiceNow expands customer value, scales innovation, and brings the power of the ServiceNow AI platform to market through a global partner ecosystem. The Executive Administrative Assistant is a critical enabler of that mission—creating focus, connectivity, productivity, and operating leverage for the GPC Leader and leadership team.

title: Sr Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Overview

The AI Application Software Engineer designs, builds, ships, and operates applications whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret user intent, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the user's behalf. In Field Service Management, this means building AI-native experiences for scheduling, dispatch, and service workflows that automate routine work, escalate exceptions, and improve customer outcomes.

This is a hands-on, forward deployed role for a senior engineer whose first instinct is AI — someone who can shape ambiguous customer problems into precise specifications, author the instructions and prompts that govern agent behavior, build the application and integrations around them, and prove through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly. This is not a machine learning or AI research role; you will not train foundation models. You own what ships, whether a human or an agent produced it.

What You Get to Do

•      Build AI-native applications. Design and ship applications built around agentic behavior across Field Service Management — scheduling, dispatch, and workflows that reason over context, automate routine work, and escalate exceptions.

•      Work AI-first in delivery. Direct coding agents to build, refactor, and test; use AI to think more sharply in front of customers; and apply it as part of everyday engineering practice rather than as a side tool.

•      Deliver forward deployed. Work embedded in customer environments, tuning instructions and evaluation sets on the ground, using AI to compress turnaround without cutting quality.

•      Author and maintain agentic instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern agent behavior — treating them as reviewed, regression-covered engineering artifacts.

•      Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic behavior. Design and operate golden datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring, CI gates, drift detection, adversarial testing, and grounding checks that make change safe.

•      Design conversational experiences. Build experiences that hold context, confirm before consequential actions, and hand off cleanly to humans.

•      Collaborate across product, UX, and documentation. Bring the AI-first instinct into cross-functional partnerships, not just your own code.

•      Own quality and safety in production. Monitor containment, hallucination, prompt injection, and data leakage, then feed failures back into specifications and evaluation sets.

Qualifications

Experience
A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production software, including hands-on delivery of AI-native application features that real users depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing AI-driven workflows, and building evaluation and testing for non-deterministic behavior is required. Experience with chat experiences is required; voice or multi-channel experience is strongly preferred. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity is required; prior forward deployed experience is an advantage.

Education
Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience.

Key competencies
•      Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing. Good to have technologies like  HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Java. 

•      AI-native application development. Hands-on experience with agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling latency, cost, and failure.
•      Agentic instruction and prompt engineering. Demonstrated skill with instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, structured outputs, grounding, citation, graceful failure, and disciplined iteration against measured outcomes.
•      Specification precision. Ability to define a problem rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements it correctly, and to judge when to solve it in code, in instructions, or by delegating.
•      Customer-facing delivery with AI-native speed. Comfort working directly with customers under real constraints, using AI to cut turnaround, and communicating capability and risk credibly to non-engineers.
•      AI safety and data handling. Working knowledge of prompt injection, data leakage, over-broad tool access, and unsafe autonomous action, translated into concrete guardrails and least-privilege controls.

Desired experience
•      Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment.
•      A platform-level view. Experience with agent runtimes, context engineering, retrieval, and memory.
•      Domain depth. Experience in Field Service Management, scheduling, or workforce management is valued but not required; the right engineer can learn the domain.
•      Evaluation and observability tooling. Experience with evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production transcripts at scale.

Job Description

Role Overview

We are seeking a Senior Manager to lead strategic readiness for both operational readiness and field readiness across our go-to-market motion. This leader brings the clarity to set direction for complex launches and the discipline to turn that direction into a clear, executable plan. You will ensure that the business processes, tools, and field teams are ready to transact, sell, position, and demo new and evolving offers, from the back office through to the customer.

The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker who can take an ambiguous launch or transformation and create clarity: what the outcome is, what it takes to get there, who needs to act, and how progress will be measured. You are scrappy yet polished, comfortable influencing without direct authority, and able to connect operational rigor with the needs of sellers and customers. You have led business process transformation, and you know how to design scalable frameworks that outlast any single launch.

What You’ll Do

Strategy and Planning

  • Partner with Product, Sales, and GTM leaders to understand strategy, value proposition, and launch objectives, and translate them into a clear readiness strategy.
  • Define the scope, sequencing, dependencies, and success criteria for each readiness effort, covering both operational and field readiness.
  • Develop detailed execution plans with clear owners, milestones, risks, and decision points, and drive them from inception to completion on time, on budget, and with quality.

Lead to Cash and Operational Readiness

  • Lead the stand-up and transformation of Lead to Cash processes, spanning quote, contract, order, billing, and renewal, and ensure transactability for new offers and business models.
  • Ensure comprehensive readiness across sales and operations processes (goal to commission, account planning, deal lifecycle) and tools (CPQ, CLM, dashboards) for all sales roles.
  • Work with Monetization, Legal, Compliance, Revenue, Sales Operations, and Deal Desk to resolve process gaps and align on how new offers get sold and closed.
  • Drive digitization and automation initiatives that improve speed, quality, and scale.

Field Readiness

  • Develop and execute field readiness plans for new and evolving offers, preparing sellers, technical sales, and demo teams to sell and position with confidence.
  • Create scalable, repeatable readiness frameworks that apply across future in-market launches, and address gaps and overlaps in enablement efforts.
  • Establish the cadence and tools that keep field readiness aligned with operational readiness, so the field is never ahead of the back office.

Measurement and Continuous Improvement

  • Define and manage leading and lagging KPIs for operational and field readiness, and drive action plans to improve them.
  • Conduct rigorous analysis to produce data-driven recommendations for leadership decisions.
  • Deliver clear progress updates to stakeholders and senior leadership.
  • Apply a customer and partner lens across the journey to identify and act on optimization opportunities.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in GTM operations, business process transformation, field readiness, sales enablement, product launches, or a related area.
  • Hands-on experience standing up or transforming Lead to Cash processes in a SaaS or enterprise environment.

  • Strong analytical, facilitation, and project management skills, with the ability to turn complex information into clear plans and recommendations.
  • Excellent executive presence and communication, with the ability to influence without direct authority and align diverse stakeholders.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and fast-paced, multi-priority environments.

We are seeking a motivated and experienced lawyer specialized in Employment Law to join our Global Employment Law team to support the continued growth of ServiceNow across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA). The role will report to the Senior Director, Global Employment Law.   

The Director, Global Employment Law, EMEA will be primarily responsible for providing legal counsel and partnership to the Global People Organization and other key internal stakeholders globally on employment law matters.  This is a unique opportunity to play a pivotal role in ServiceNow’s expanding legal team and to work on challenging legal issues in an exciting, fast-paced environment.  

What you get to do in this role:  

  • Help us build a culture of high performance and great inclusion. Deliver business oriented, risk-based advice and counsel on the full range of employment law issues including: hiring, separations and dismissals, employee relations issues, restructurings, works councils and collective consultation, compensation and benefits, leaves of absence, global workforce innovation and culture, workplace investigations and employee relations, and employee privacy matters. Fully understanding the legal requirements is the starting point – treating people fairly and creating an amazing working environment is the end point  

  • Partner with our Global People Organization to create and revise global and locally compliant policies and procedures consistent with our values  

  • Partner with our Ethics & Compliance, Employee Relations, and Global People teams to conduct prompt, thorough investigations into employee concerns

  • Advise and collaborate with the Global People Organization to develop and implement global programs initiatives  

  • Develop and deliver best in class employee related trainings  

  • Manage employment claims and litigation matters across EMEA, including selecting and managing outside counsel  

  • Partner and collaborate with other members of the Global Employment Law team on global projects and issues  

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to EMEA senior leadership on complex, high-risk employment matters, including multi-country restructurings, M&A and M&A integration, workforce transformation, and executive matters 

  • Deliver strategic advice and counsel on the development and deployment of AI tools in the employment lifecycle, including advising on works council consultations and agreements 

  • Contribute to the development of ServiceNow's Legal Services Delivery applications, envisioning, creating, and deploying workflows on the ServiceNow Platform  

  • Monitor and maintain knowledge of changes in EMEA employment laws and regulations and industry practices that impact our business, and provide practical advice and support to the business regarding the same

  • Experience in leveraging and critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, and problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry.

  • A law degree with strong academic credentials   

  • Fully qualified lawyer in good standing in a relevant European jurisdiction (preferably France, Germany,Ireland or the UK)

  • Deep employment law experience across a variety of EMEA jurisdictions, including leading works council and collective consultation processes, and a desire to develop and expand expertise

Your mandate is to convert ServiceNow's next-generation, AI-native CRM vision into consistent, repeatable pre-sales motions that win—at speed and at scale. 

You will re-establish a tight connection between the field and CRM product, build the next generation of pre-sales talent around the Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) model, and lead the shift from a demo-centric to a proof-of-value (POV) centric go-to-market motion. Own the number – drive CRM NNACV growth

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

As a Senior Staff Engineer in HRSD, you set the technical direction for model-driven capability across the HR domain, the agentic and conversational experiences that interpret employee, manager, and HR agent intent, reason over profile, case, catalog, policy, and knowledge context, and act on the user's behalf. Your unit of ownership is the architecture, standards, and evaluation infrastructure that let multiple teams ship those experiences safely — not a single feature set. 

This is not an ML research role; you do not train foundation models. It is also distinct from traditional full-stack staff work, where systems follow deterministic logic. Two things shape the job: much of the load-bearing logic lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, context, tool descriptions, guardrails — and must be engineered with the same discipline as code; and because behavior is probabilistic, correctness is established through evaluation at scale, not fixed assertions. 

What You'll Own 

AI architecture for the domain. How agents are decomposed and composed, where reasoning happens, how context is assembled and bounded, how tools are exposed, and how autonomy is delegated. Own the multi-release calls: model selection and migration, orchestration approach, build-versus-adopt, and the cost/latency/quality tradeoffs behind each. 

The autonomy boundary. Decide as domain policy which HR actions an agent may take, which require a human decision point, and which no agent should attempt. Anything changing pay, employment status, restricted records, or employee-relations matters requires a human in the path by construction — build the mechanisms that make those constraints structural. 

The shared instruction and tool description surface. HRSD ships as product; customers configure, extend, and override this surface on their own instances. Treat it as a versioned contract with upgrade-safe extension points, deprecation paths, and compatibility guarantees. 

Evaluation as infrastructure. Own the golden datasets, multi-turn suites, judge calibration, CI gates, and drift detection that let teams change behavior safely. Extend coverage to HR-specific failure classes: access-boundary violations, cross-scope leakage, jurisdictional and policy-variant correctness. 

Production quality and safety. Observability for containment, hallucination rate, tool-selection error, unsafe action, and injection vectors from user-supplied content entering agent context. Because HR conversation content is itself restricted, design diagnosis that works without exposing what was said. 

AI-assisted engineering standards. Convert ambiguous problems into testable specs; define what accountable agent-assisted delivery looks like for the domain — specification standards, review expectations, verification harnesses — and hold the line on it. 

Hands-on where it matters. The hard integration, the risky migration, the prototype that settles an architectural argument, the incident nobody else can unblock. 

Partner across functions. Collaborate efficiently with product, engineering, design to co-create scalable AI solutions and translate business needs into robust technical designs. 

Qualifications

What You Bring:

7+ years of software engineering, with a record of technical direction adopted beyond your immediate team. 

Direct, hands-on experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing autonomous workflows, and building the evaluation that verifies them. 

Production experience with LLM APIs, retrieval-grounded features, agent orchestration, tool and function calling, and structured output enforcement — including at least one model or orchestration migration carried through production. 

Entitlement-aware data handling: per-user access enforcement in retrieval and tool layers, scope separation between roles, and handling of restricted records under audit. 

Evaluation experience used by engineers other than yourself: dataset curation, judge calibration, CI gating, drift detection. 

Strong command of system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing across front-end, server-side, and relational data work with a high quality mindset. 

Effective, accountable use of AI coding assistants and agents. 

On-call and incident-command experience on customer-facing systems, including ownership of the systemic fixes that followed. 

Experience in software stack including Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, React and demonstrated ability to quickly learn new tools and frameworks. 

Bachelor's degree in CS, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 

Preferred 

HR domain depth: case management, employee journey and lifecycle, or payroll/benefits/leave/absence sufficient to set requirements. 

Integration with core HR, payroll, or benefits systems of record, including reconciliation and eventual-consistency patterns. 

Contribution in a Forward deployment model to champion customer adoption.

Cette approche unifiée permet à des processus critiques et à grande échelle, allant de l’intégration client, des plaintes, de la gestion des fraudes et des litiges, jusqu’aux successions, aux exceptions commerciales, à la gestion des courtiers et des négociants en valeurs mobilières, etc., de s’appuyer sur une information uniforme, une IA prédictive et une efficacité opérationnelle inégalée.

Ce que vous piloterez : CRM et IA au service du succès stratégique

Votre mission consistera à transformer la complexité sectorielle en valeur d’affaires mesurable :

  • Stratégie et exécution à l’échelle de l’entreprise :
  • Gestion de comptes : Élaborer et mettre en œuvre une stratégie de territoire axée sur des cas d’usage à forte valeur. Apporter une contribution pointue, propre à chaque secteur, lors de la planification des comptes, en veillant à ce que les comptes cibles et les cas d’usage soient alignés sur le potentiel de retour sur investissement élevé de nos solutions CRM propulsées par l’IA.

  • Cibler et valider les occasions CRM et IA : Prospecter et développer le pipeline dans les comptes CRM et faire croître les partenariats CRM existants grâce à une vente consultative, incluant notamment des séances d’information pour dirigeants (EBC), des ateliers de découverte et des projets pilotes de cas d’usage.

  • Défendre la valeur transformationnelle : collaborer avec les équipes de comptes, les partenaires d’implantation de solutions et les revendeurs pour conclure de nouvelles ventes, afin d’aider les dirigeants d’entreprise à améliorer l’efficacité opérationnelle et l’expérience client.
  • Soutien aux ventes et formation des équipes :

########

You will be instrumental in overseeing the market success and expansion of ServiceNow's next-generation CRM and AI products, positioning them as the essential backbone for enterprise-wide digital transformation. 

Our CRM products are not just stand-alone tools; they are built upon our market-leading Service Management platform, creating a single, intelligent source of truth. This unified approach allows mission-critical, enterprise-scale processes—from customer onboarding, complaints, fraud and disputes management to decedent, trade exceptions, broker/dealer servicing, etc —to execute uniform information, predictive AI, and unmatched operational efficiency.

Job Description

As a trusted C-Suite / executive level advisor on ServiceNow offerings, the Senior Customer Success Executive owns the post-sale customer relationship, aiming to increase customer satisfaction and drive retention through Impact delivery. Senior CSEs are experienced individuals who bring a consultative, problem-solving approach to partnering with senior customer stakeholders to derive value from our platforms. This role drives business transformation by maximizing the long-term strategic value of ServiceNow and ensuring that every aspect of the customer’s platform and capability are ready for expansion. 

They provide strategic direction and mentorship to both customers and ServiceNow teams managing complex, multi-workstream programs. They play a pivotal role in resolving escalations and mitigating risks, ensuring adoption and usage is maintained at healthy levels. Senior CSEs focus on ensuring the customer recognizes the value of the ServiceNow Platform at all levels and stages, facilitating a smooth path to both renewal and up- and cross-sell. 

Overall, Senior CSEs are responsible for fostering the relationship with C-suite level stakeholders in a smaller number of strategically important Impact accounts, with the aim of increasing customer satisfaction and driving retention and upgrades, where applicable. 

Job Responsibilities:

  • Lead high-complexity transformations in our largest and most strategic customers, ensuring all ServiceNow Customer Excellence roles align and deliver in accordance with governance frameworks, customer objectives, and organizational priorities; ultimately chaperoning Impact value management and demonstrating strategic oversight.

  • Provide prescriptive guidance on internal project/program governance and help the customer create the appropriate governance models and ensure adherence. 
  • Help the customer identify incidents where contractual SLAs were missed and take necessary action. 
  • Improve overall customer satisfaction, as well as the satisfaction of their internal customers.

    4. Security Operations
    5. Customer Service Management
    6. IT Processes

    8. IT Portfolio, Program and Project Management

  • Independently leverages AI to optimize workflows, tailor customer solutions, and inform strategic decisions. 
  • Articulates AI system design, ethical implications, and platform use cases clearly, guiding peers and stakeholders in responsible, value-driven AI adoption.

Job Description

The role 

This senior principal solution architect is a functional and technical expert who consults with customers on implementing ServiceNow’s Security and Risk solutions in line with leading practices, accelerating customer business outcomes and helping build the practice. The role is laser-focused on the most relevant customer challenges. It supports sales cycles, engages directly with customers and partners, and advocates for customer needs within ServiceNow (Product Management, Customer & Partner Excellence, Training & Certification). 

The solution architect brings architectural guidance, industry business acumen, deep product expertise, innovation, and knowledge capital to customers and partners. 

Responsibilities 

  • Lead pre-sales activities: sales presentations, solutioning and scoping workshops, SOW development with clear deliverables and effort estimates, scope definition and change order triggers, and engagement sizing with Services Account Executives and Sales team members. 
  • Serve as a lead member of the engagement team, focused on connecting Security and Risk workflow applications to the customer’s technology landscape while advising on governance leading practices. 
  • Engage senior leadership, including CXOs, on implementation roadmap and change management. 
  • Partner with the Platform Architect team to surface proactive platform risks in customer landscapes. 
  • Act as practice director on marquee accounts for Security and Risk, leading delivery teams, providing oversight and technical expertise, and owning adherence to delivery standards. 
  • Design and deliver Security and Risk solutions with a technical architecture built for long-term success, following ServiceNow technical standards and leading practices.

  • Experience with cross-functional solutions and architectural foundations in large, heavily regulated enterprises such as FSI and HCLS. 
  • Experience applying AI to work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving: AI-powered tools, workflow automation, AI-driven insights, or the impact of AI on the function or industry.

  • Ability to work with technical and non-technical customers, gather requirements, analyze information, and design comprehensive solutions. 
  • Ability to produce visually rich conceptual design documents for audiences of varying business and technical aptitude. 
  • Experience running solution presentations and securing customer acceptance of solution designs. 
  • Strength in building trust and engaging remote or in-person audiences. 
  • Aptitude for communicating complex concepts through visualization and modeling, including wireframes, workflows, and diagrams. 
  • Creativity and comfort running projects independently, with success driving complex issues to resolution. 
  • Collaborative working style. 
  • Breadth across leading technology software platforms. 
  • A passion for learning new technologies and working on projects that push the platform’s capabilities.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the team

The Conversational AI team at ServiceNow builds the core platform behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI experience. We are a group of applied scientists and software engineers working at the intersection of research and production. Our work spans the full stack that makes Otto capable: agent orchestration, including harness engineering, prompt tuning, agent skills, policy design, and quality evaluation across languages; the A2A and MCP protocols that let agents collaborate and connect to tools; background channels and conversational triggers that bring agents into action; AI-native licensing and pricing; and the central caching layer that connects the ServiceNow platform to the services powering Otto.

We are seeking a Staff AI-Native DevOps Engineer to join a new DevOps practice within the Conversational AI team. You will own the build, deployment, and reliability of the systems behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI platform, from commit through production across our SaaS environments. Your work will span CI/CD pipelines, release automation, infrastructure on Kubernetes, observability, and the operational tooling that lets agent orchestration, MCP and A2A services, and the central caching layer ship safely and frequently. You will partner closely with applied scientists and software engineers to make AI-native delivery repeatable, measurable, and secure. This role combines deep expertise in cloud infrastructure, containerization, orchestration, and infrastructure as code with a practical understanding of how ML and LLM-based services behave in production, and a bias toward pragmatic engineering with measurable impact on deployment velocity and service reliability.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Deep expertise in designing, building, and operating scalable, reliable, and secure cloud-native applications and infrastructure.
  • Strong software engineering skills, with experience developing infrastructure tooling and automation using Go, Python, or similar languages.
  • Experience leading complex infrastructure initiatives, establishing engineering best practices, and driving adoption across multiple teams.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex distributed systems issues and drive improvements in performance, reliability, and operational efficiency.
  • Strong understanding of modern AI technologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, and agentic architectures, with the ability to apply these concepts to engineering and operational challenges.
  • An AI-native engineering mindset, proactively leveraging AI tools and automation to accelerate development, improve operational efficiency, and deliver more intelligent, resilient systems.

DevOps:

  • Deploy, scale, and operate distributed microservices in production Kubernetes environments, including managing application lifecycle, networking, security, and service reliability.
  • Design and implement infrastructure automation using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Kubernetes-native tooling, including Terraform, Ansible, Helm, and Kubernetes Operators.
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows using tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Tekton, and ArgoCD to automate testing, deployment, and release management.
  • Implement observability, monitoring, and incident response practices, performing root cause analysis and driving remediation to improve availability, fault tolerance, and operational resilience.
  • Architect and optimize cloud infrastructure across public and private cloud environments, with an emphasis on security, scalability, cost efficiency, and operational simplicity.

AI skills:

Artificial intelligence strategy is a critical skill at your level — it applies to how you build and to what you build. 

  • Confident use of AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot or Cursor, paired with the critical eye to review AI-generated code as rigorously as any other — catching logic errors, security anti-patterns, and missed edge cases rather than treating model output as production-ready. 
  • AI-assisted debugging and trace analysis, and a clear understanding of the data privacy rules governing what goes into a prompt.
  • Understanding of LLM-powered application architectures, including model inference, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool calling, and agentic workflows, with an awareness of their infrastructure, scalability, and reliability implications.
  • Ability to deploy, operate, and troubleshoot AI-powered services in production, including managing model API integrations, observability, latency, resource utilization, and operational costs.

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or related experience.
  • 6+ years of experience deploying and operating containerized applications and distributed services in production environments. 
  • 4+ years of hands-on experience with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, and infrastructure automation.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language, such as Go, Python, or Bash, with experience building production-grade automation and tooling.
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools in software engineering workflows, with demonstrated ability to validate, debug, and safely integrate AI-generated code.
  • Working knowledge of LLMs, Generative AI, and agentic AI concepts, including their integration patterns and operational considerations.

Preferred requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in software engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or platform engineering.
  • Extensive experience architecting and operating Kubernetes-based SaaS platforms at scale, including multi-service deployments and complex production environments.
  • Experience developing Kubernetes Operators, custom controllers, or other Kubernetes-native automation to manage application lifecycle and infrastructure operations.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership in driving cross-team infrastructure initiatives, improving production reliability, and establishing scalable platform engineering practices.
  • Hands-on experience deploying, integrating, or operating LLM-powered applications or agentic systems in production environments. Experience building AI-enabled infrastructure automation, observability, incident diagnosis, or remediation workflows to improve platform reliability and engineering productivity.
