Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Group Vice President, Enterprise Verticals Sales US, will be a pivotal leader responsible for driving the overall strategy, execution, and growth of ServiceNow's Manufacturing, Transportation and Energy business across the United States. This executive will lead a team dedicated to serving these verticals within the US, ensuring that ServiceNow's platform helps these critical industries deliver better services, optimize operations, and achieve their mission objectives. The GVP will be accountable for exceeding revenue targets, expanding market share, building strong customer relationships at the executive level, and fostering a high-performance sales culture specific to these industries.

Responsibilities:

  • Strategic Leadership: Develop and execute a comprehensive Manufacturing, Transportation and Energy sector sales strategy aligned with ServiceNow's overall corporate objectives. Identify new market opportunities, emerging trends, and competitive landscapes within these sectors.
  • Revenue Growth & Performance: Drive aggressive year-over-year revenue growth for these industries. Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual sales quotas and KPIs. Manage a robust pipeline, forecast accurately, and implement effective sales methodologies.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Recruit, hire, mentor, and develop a world-class sales organization. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, and customer obsession.
  • Customer & Stakeholder Relationships: Build and maintain strong, executive-level relationships with key customers, partners, and industry influencers across the US. Act as a trusted advisor, understanding their complex challenges and positioning ServiceNow's value proposition effectively.
  • Go-to-Market Execution: Collaborate closely with product management, marketing, professional services, and other internal teams to ensure a cohesive go-to-market strategy for the these industries.  Provide market feedback to inform product development and solution innovation.
  • Operational Excellence: Implement best practices for sales operations, including territory planning,  quota setting, sales process optimization, and CRM utilization. Ensure data-driven decision-making across the sales organization.
  • Compliance & Governance: Ensure all sales activities adhere to strict ethical standards and company policies, specifically within the US.
  • Partnership Ecosystem: Work strategically with the regional partner ecosystem to leverage their capabilities and expand ServiceNow's reach within the Manufacturing, Transportation and Energy industries.

Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in enterprise software sales
  • 10+ years specifically leading large-scale Industries sales organizations (Manufacturing, Transportation, Energy) within the US.
  • Proven track record of consistently exceeding multi-hundred-million-dollar sales quotas and driving significant revenue growth in complex environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to build, scale, and lead high-performing, geographically dispersed sales teams within the US.
  • Exceptional executive-level communication, presentation, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret sales performance data, identify trends, and develop actionable strategies.
  • Ability to travel within the US as required.
  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Sales, Marketing, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior experience selling cloud-based SaaS solutions and IT workflow automation platforms.
  • Experience in a rapidly growing, high-growth technology company.
  • Familiarity with the ServiceNow platform and its capabilities.

Leadership Competencies:

  • Strategic Vision: Ability to define and articulate a clear vision for the business.
  • Execution Focus: Drives results with a strong sense of urgency and accountability.
  • Talent Development: Committed to developing and retaining top talent.
  • Customer Centricity: Puts the customer at the heart of all decisions and actions.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively across organizational boundaries to achieve shared goals.
  • Integrity: Operates with the highest level of ethics and transparency.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $230,950 - $392,600, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. The Opportunity:

ServiceNow is looking for a Vice President of Corporate and Product Public Relations to lead all earned media strategy across the Americas, spanning the United States, Canada, and Latin America. This is a senior executive role with enterprise-wide accountability for how ServiceNow is perceived externally as an AI leader that makes the world work better..

Reporting to the Chief Communications Officer, you will own the full PR agenda across corporate reputation, product storytelling, executive visibility, and crisis and issues management for the Americas region. You will lead a high-performing team of PR professionals, manage agency relationships, drive AI tool use, and serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership, including the CEO, on all matters of public narrative.

This role sits at the intersection of corporate and product communications, requiring someone who can connect financial momentum and brand reputation to product innovation and market positioning in one coherent voice.

What You'll Do:

Regional PR Leadership

  • Own and execute the integrated PR strategy for the Americas, aligning corporate and product narratives across US, Canada, and LATAM markets.
  • Build and scale a high-performing PR team, setting clear performance expectations, coaching talent, and fostering a culture of accountability and creative excellence.
  • Leverage AI tools and emerging technologies to drive smarter, faster communications and set the standard for how the team works in an AI-first environment.
  • Manage agency relationships across the region, including scope, performance, and budget.
  • Develop annual operating plans, budgets, and KPIs tied to reputation, share of voice, executive visibility, and business impact.
  • Experience in a Marcom function that embraced leadership across both the marketing and communications functions

Corporate Communications

  • Lead development and execution of corporate PR strategy that positions ServiceNow as a market leader in AI-powered enterprise transformation.
  • Drive proactive media outreach across top-tier technology, business, financial, and general press in the Americas.
  • Own regional financial communications including earnings support, investor narrative alignment, and regulatory disclosures, in partnership with Finance and Legal.
  • Manage issues and crisis communications with speed, poise, and rigor; maintain regional crisis playbooks and lead scenario planning.

Product and Innovation PR

  • Build and execute product PR strategy across ServiceNow workflows, the Now Platform, and AI and GenAI offerings, tying product launches to broader corporate and market narratives.
  • Partner with Product, Marketing, and Sales to drive integrated launch and go-to-market campaigns that maximize coverage and audience engagement.
  • Translate complex technology into compelling, accessible stories for business and technology media across the region.
  • Develop press materials, messaging frameworks, and content that clearly articulate product value, customer outcomes, and competitive differentiation.

Executive Visibility and Counsel

  • Earn credibility and trust, and serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the executive leadership team on reputation management, narrative positioning, and external communications.
  • Build executive public profiles for regional and global leaders through strategic media placements, speaking opportunities, and thought leadership.
  • Prepare senior executives for media engagements, including message development, briefings, and coaching.

Storytelling and Media Relations

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with editors, reporters, and influencers across tech, business, and industry media throughout the Americas.
  • Craft and drive multi-dimensional narratives that connect ServiceNow's corporate vision to product innovation, customer success, and business impact.
  • Serve as regional spokesperson when appropriate.
  • Track, analyze, and report on PR performance using data-driven insights to continually refine strategy and demonstrate business impact.

Qualifications

  • 15+ years of progressive communications and public relations leadership, with significant experience in technology, SaaS, or high-growth enterprise software.
  • Demonstrated success leading both corporate and product communications functions, with the ability to integrate them into a unified regional strategy.
  • Deep familiarity with the Americas media landscape across US, Canada, and Latin American markets; cultural fluency required.
  • Experience with financial and earnings communications, M&A, and executive transitions.
  • Proven crisis communications experience with the ability to move quickly and decisively under pressure.
  • Bachelor's degree required in Communications, Journalism, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

Leadership

  • Track record of building and scaling high-performing, diverse PR teams in matrixed, global organizations.
  • Demonstrated fluency with AI-powered communications tools and a track record of applying them to improve team productivity, content quality, and decision-making.
  • Ability to influence senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners without direct authority.
  • Experience managing external agencies and large communications budgets.

Media and Storytelling

  • Extensive media network across top-tier technology, business, and financial press in the Americas.
  • Exceptional writer and storyteller, with the ability to translate complex AI and platform technology into narratives that resonate across audiences.
  • Deep fluency in AI, cloud, and enterprise software trends, with the ability to position ServiceNow's products in a competitive landscape.

Strategic Mindset

  • Comfortable operating at the executive level while maintaining the ability to roll up sleeves and drive hands-on execution.
  • Strong business acumen, with the ability to connect communications strategy to commercial outcomes.
  • Skilled scenario planner who anticipates reputational risk and acts proactively.

Job Description

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join the AppSec engineering team in Armis R&D. 

The team builds Armis Centrix for Application Security, an AI-native AppSec product built from the ground up over the past year and now growing into a core product line. You get the best of both worlds: a small, autonomous team that owns its product end to end, backed by the data, expertise, and stability of Armis and ServiceNow engineering. If you love taking a product from its first customers to enterprise scale, own outcomes end to end, and raise the bar for the people around you, this is for you. 

What You'll Do 

  • Own Your Area: Take complex, open-ended problems from design through production, hands-on in architecture, design, and the critical paths of the codebase, with the accountability that comes with it. 
  • Build Agentic AppSec: Design and build LLM-based agents and pipelines that analyze real-world codebases at scale: orchestration, tool use, context engineering, and the deterministic components that do what models shouldn't. 
  • Make AI Trustworthy: Practice evaluation-driven development: the evaluation harness, golden datasets, regression gates in CI, and cost and latency tracking, so every pipeline change is measured before it ships. 
  • Own the Backend & AI Architecture: Design robust, multi-tenant microservice cloud environments with security by design as the default. 
  • Deliver on Commitments: Design, estimate, and deliver your work as clear, estimated tasks you own end to end. 
  • Raise the Bar: Review designs and code, mentor engineers around you, and help set the team's engineering standards. 
  • Engage Beyond the Code: Work directly with product, customers, support, and R&D architecture to gather real-world insight, unblock fast, and align technical direction with the business. 
  • Collaborate Globally: Work closely with engineers and stakeholders across Israel, North America, and India. 

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of deep backend/systems experience, strong Python, and real production experience in a multi-tenant microservice cloud environment. 

  • Strong advantage: hands-on experience building LLM-based agents or agentic pipelines in production, and evaluating them: golden datasets, benchmark, regression gates, cost and latency at scale. 

  • A track record of owning outcomes end to end, including a commitment that went wrong and what you did about it. 

  • A security engineering mindset: tenant isolation, access control, and secure design are non-negotiable to you. 

  •  An All-Around Player: independent, execution-focused, and happy to build whatever it takes. 

Excellent English for working effectively across time zones.

What you get to do in this role:

We are looking for a Technical Customer Success Manager (TCSM) to join our growing Customer Success Team, who are a key in helping our valued customers achieve their strategic objectives and obtain maximum value from their investment in their Armis Platform. This will include helping in aligning new use cases to the CISO goals, and identify growth opportunities by informing the customer of our latest innovations, capabilities, and products and match these to the clients’ business goals.   • Contribute to thought leadership and point-of-view documents, knowledge base articles, and other documentation to make ServiceNow's AICT capabilities more accessible to customers and partners

  • Customer-facing advisory or consulting experience with proven ability to translate technical capabilities into business outcomes

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with ability to work independently or as part of a team
  • A strong propensity for use & innovation across various AI tools

Additionally, one of the following:

  • Deep ServiceNow platform expertise (5+ years) with hands-on implementation across multiple product suites; CSA certification required, CIS or CAD expected within first year; OR

  • Hands-on experience implementing ServiceNow AI Control Tower, GRC, or related governance and risk applications
  • Familiarity with enterprise AI/ML platforms, such as Azure AI, AWS, or Google Cloud, and how organizations deploy AI at scale
  • Experience supporting new product launches or early adopter programs for enterprise software
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies and experience working in an Agile environment
  • Strong industry connections within the EMEA AI governance and compliance community

Job Description

As Director of Pricing & Packaging Strategy for the EmployeeWorks Business Unit, you’ll own how our AI products are priced, packaged, and brought to market. You’ll partner with Product, Data Science, Marketing, Sales, Finance, and executive leadership to turn pricing into a growth lever, building models and offers that drive acquisition, expand existing customers, and protect retention. This role sits at the center of product strategy and go-to-market, and it shapes how customers experience the value of EmployeeWorks from first deal through renewal. 

What you’ll do 

Pricing strategy development and innovation 

  • Partner with Product, Data Science, Marketing, Sales, Finance, and executives to build pricing models for every new or repackaged SKU. 

  • Partner with ServiceNow’s central pricing team to keep EmployeeWorks pricing and packaging aligned with company-wide pricing strategy. 

  • Develop and maintain pricing strategies that align with BU and company objectives, grounded in primary research, financial modeling, stakeholder interviews, and competitive research. 

  • Design pricing, bundling, and offer strategies, along with the sales plays that bring them to market, to maximize customer acquisition, retention, and revenue. 

Consumption pricing strategy 

  • Own the consumption pricing strategy for the BU, including setting the rate card for Assist consumption. 

  • Propose rate card and consumption pricing changes in partnership with the central pricing team. 

  • Partner with Data Science and Engineering on Assist metering telemetry, so usage is measured accurately and billed consistently. 

  • Drive token spend analysis and optimization to protect margins as customer usage scales. 

  • Own consumption tracking, analysis, and insights for the business, turning usage trends into pricing, packaging, and forecasting decisions. 

Go-to-market alignment 

  • Align monetization efforts across Sales, Marketing, and post-sales success teams so pricing translates into revenue and retention. 

  • Build and maintain a centralized pricing excellence hub that equips sales and renewals teams to price with confidence. 

  • Help sales build glide paths to different SKU options that drive upsells and renewals. 

  • Manage pricing strategy across direct, partner, and reseller channels, ensuring consistent execution and profitability across all of them, including third-party partnerships. 

Insights and analytics 

  • Build frameworks to monitor pricing performance and present insights and recommendations to senior leadership. 

  • Create financial models and analyses to assess the impact of pricing decisions, and design experiments to test pricing hypotheses. 

Competitive intelligence and market analysis 

  • Lead pricing research, including competitor analysis and market benchmarking, to keep EmployeeWorks competitively positioned. 

Qualifications

What you bring to the table 

  • 7+ years of experience in pricing strategy, product monetization, or financial analysis, ideally in SaaS or AI. 

  • Deep expertise in financial modeling, revenue optimization, and strategic analysis. 

  • A track record of pricing decisions that delivered measurable business impact. 

  • Strong leadership presence and experience influencing senior stakeholders toward business outcomes. 

  • Proven operator in cross-functional environments: strong prioritization instincts, able to build consensus and drive results without direct authority. 

  • Strong judgment about when to act independently and when to escalate, with the ability to navigate ambiguity. 

  • Comfort operating in a highly collaborative, fast-paced environment. 

  • Proven ability to thrive in a highly dynamic environment where written guides and playbooks are sparse and changes occur nearly daily: you create structure where none exists, ramp quickly, ask sharp questions, stay current without being told, and keep partners and leadership aligned as things shift. 

  • Excellent communication skills, with a talent for making complex pricing concepts clear to non-financial audiences. 

  • Fluency in AI, with the ability to translate engineering and product concepts for non-technical stakeholders and represent EmployeeWorks products to central pricing, product management, and GTM teams.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Job Description

The Role

We're building the runtime infrastructure that powers Moveworks' AI agents — the systems that orchestrate, execute, and deliver agent responses to millions of enterprise users in real time. This is not an ML role. This is a distributed systems engineering role at the heart of the agentic AI wave.

Our AI agents can plan, execute multi-step workflows, call tools, wait on human input, and resume — all while maintaining correctness, observability, and low latency. The systems that make this possible are what you'll build and own.


What you get to do in this role:

  • Agent orchestration engine — A state machine that manages long-running agent sessions, coordinating planning, execution, and user interaction across multiple LLM calls and tool invocations
  • Distributed session management — Lease-based ownership using DynamoDB conditional writes, heartbeat protocols, and crash recovery via checkpointing
  • Event-driven message pipeline — SQS FIFO queues for ordered delivery, Kafka consumers for event processing, and real-time streaming via gRPC and Socket.IO
  • Structured concurrency — Python asyncio TaskGroups running multiple concurrent tasks per session (message polling, lease heartbeats, output publishing, orchestrator execution) with fail-fast semantics and graceful cancellation
  • Observability infrastructure — OpenTelemetry instrumentation, distributed trace context propagation across async boundaries, custom span lifecycle management for sessions that span minutes
  • Caching and state layers — Redis, DynamoDB KV stores with per-org/per-bot scoping, batch read optimization, and hot-reload configuration

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

You should have deep experience in at least 3 of these areas:

  • Distributed systems: consistency models, idempotency, exactly-once delivery, distributed locking/leasing
  • Concurrent/async programming: Python asyncio, Go goroutines, structured concurrency, cancellation handling
  • Event-driven architectures: message queues (SQS, Kafka), pub/sub, backpressure, delivery guarantees
  • Database systems for infrastructure: DynamoDB (conditional writes, transactions), Redis (connection pooling, pub/sub)
  • Observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, span context propagation, Prometheus metrics
  • gRPC/protobuf: streaming RPCs, service interface design, error handling patterns

Required:

  • 10+ years building production backend/infrastructure systems
  • Strong in Python or Go (ideally both)
  • Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale
  • Comfort with ambiguity — these are novel problems without textbook solutions

title: Solution Sales Executive - Data & Analytics
descriptionHtml:
企業概要

ServiceNowの歩みは2004年、陽光あふれるカリフォルニア州サンディエゴで始まりました。現在、ServiceNowはグローバル市場をリードし、Fortune 500®企業の85％を含む8,100社以上のお客様に、革新的なAI Platformテクノロジーを提供しています。インテリジェントなクラウドベースのプラットフォームは、人、システム、プロセスをシームレスにつなぎ、よりスマートに、より速く、より良人が活き活きと働ける環境を組織が実現できるよう支援しています。まだまだ私たちの旅は始まったばかりです。共にServiceNowから世界を変えてみませんか？

求人内容

Data & Analytics Solution Sales Executive（SSE）は、AI、データ、アナリティクスを通じてお客様のビジネスを変革するための技術的知見を備えた、プロフェッショナルなデータ＆アナリティクス営業人材向けのポジションです。ServiceNowのD&Aビジネス形成において重要な役割を担い、ServiceNow AI Platform上で「インサイトからアクションへ」を実現する、刺激的かつ変革的なユースケースに取り組みます。

このポジションは、ディスカバリーセッションをリードし、バリューベースのセリングを活用しながら、お客様固有の優先事項とユースケースを通じて、測定可能なビジネス成果を提供していきます。またSSEには、プレゼンテーションやデモを行い、お客様がServiceNowのD&Aソリューションへの投資に確信を持てるよう支援する技術的な対応力が必要です。

【主な役割】

  • コアのAccount Executiveと共同で主担当を務め、商談創出から受注、継続的な活用まで、D&Aのセールスサイクルをエンドツーエンドでリードする。
  • 担当アカウントに対して、D&Aポートフォリオ全体（Workflow Data Fabric、RaptorDB Pro、Data Apps、Autonomous Analytics）を担当し、販売する。
  • ServiceNowのD&Aソリューションを、お客様のAI、リアルタイムアナリティクス、データ戦略の基盤として位置付ける戦略的なD&Aアカウントプランを策定する。特に既存ServiceNow顧客における新規ビジネスの創出に注力する。
  • データ、アナリティクス、AIのリーダーに対し、ディスカバリー、価値ベースの対話、技術プレゼンテーション、デモをリードし、優先事項や課題を明らかにするとともに、AI活用に向けたデータのモダナイゼーション施策を加速する。
  • CDAO（Chief Data and Analytics Officer）を含むお客様の技術・データ担当エグゼクティブ、データエンジニアリング、データガバナンス、アナリティクスの各部門に加え、ServiceNow Platform OwnerおよびCIOとの関係を構築し、認知向上と意思決定への影響力を高める。

資格

  • D&Aセールスを中心とする3年以上のフィールドセールス経験。
  • AI、データ、アナリティクスに関する技術的な対応力。エグゼクティブ、ServiceNow Platform Owner、データ＆アナリティクスのリーダーに対して、信頼性のあるディスカバリー、価値訴求、ユースケース特定を行い、プレゼンテーションとデモを実施できること。
  • 従量課金型モデルの経験、および初回販売後のお客様の活用拡大を推進した経験。
  • 自ら進んで行動し、実務にも深く関与できるソートリーダーとして、スピード感のあるマトリクス型の製品・営業・GTM環境で業務を遂行できること。
  • 技術部門とビジネス部門の双方のステークホルダーに対する、優れたコミュニケーション能力と関係構築力。
  • 主要な購買担当者に加えて、第二の購買担当者またはインフルエンサーを開拓するなど、アカウント内で複数の部門や関係者との接点を構築した実績。

その他の情報

  • AI関連ソリューションの提案経験。
  • Tableau、ThoughtSpot、Power BI、Qlik、Oracle AnalyticsなどのアナリティクスまたはBIの知見または販売経験。
  • クラウドデータウェアハウス、データ統合、ガバナンスを含むモダンデータプラットフォームに関する知見。
  • Databricks、Snowflake、Palantirの知見または販売経験、およびより広範なデータ市場への理解。
  • 英語力

Job Description

The Team 

The Architecture Consulting & Engineering Services (ACES) team is a security-focused consulting and engineering organization that partners with many of ServiceNow's largest and most highly regulated customers. We help security teams understand, evaluate, and securely adopt the ServiceNow platform, AI capabilities, and emerging technologies. 

Our mission is to establish ServiceNow as a trusted security partner by delivering deep technical guidance, security architecture expertise, threat modeling, reference architectures, and customer-facing security engineering engagement. We operate at the intersection of Security, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to accelerate platform adoption while ensuring customers can meet their security, compliance, and risk-management objectives. 

The Role 

We are seeking an experienced Applied Security Engineer to join the ACES team. 

This is not a traditional consulting role, nor is it a traditional product security role. We are looking for a hands-on security practitioner who can dive deep into cloud-native architectures, analyze distributed systems, validate security controls, conduct threat modeling exercises, and communicate effectively with customer security teams, architects, engineers, CISOs, and executives. 

You will work directly with Fortune 500 organizations, including some of the world's largest financial services and healthcare institutions, helping them securely adopt ServiceNow platform capabilities, AI solutions, cloud services, and emerging technologies. 

Success in this role requires technical depth, customer credibility, and the ability to translate complex security concepts into practical architectural guidance. 

What You Get To Do In This Role 

  • Partner directly with customer security, architecture, engineering, risk, compliance, and executive stakeholders to address security concerns and accelerate platform adoption. 
  • Develop customer-facing security reference architectures that clearly articulate trust boundaries, data flows, identity models, encryption controls, and shared responsibility models. 
  • Perform threat modeling exercises for ServiceNow products, AI services, integrations, and customer deployment architectures. 
  • Analyze security architectures across cloud-native and distributed systems environments. 
  • Lead security deep dives covering networking, identity, encryption, data protection, application security, and AI security controls. 
  • Evaluate customer security requirements and map them to ServiceNow platform capabilities and industry best practices. 
  • Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, Product Security, and Architecture teams to identify capability gaps and advocate for customer-driven improvements. 
  • Build scalable artifacts including architecture patterns, deployment guides, implementation accelerators, technical whitepapers, detection content, and security design documentation. 
  • Assess integrations involving AI, cloud services, APIs, Kubernetes environments, data platforms, and third-party technologies. 
  • Help define secure deployment patterns for emerging AI capabilities including agents, model integrations, governance controls, and data protection mechanisms. 

  • Represent ServiceNow security architecture and best practices during customer workshops, architecture reviews, executive briefings, and security assessments. 

Qualifications

To Be Successful In This Role You Have 

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in security engineering, security architecture, cloud security, application security, product security, or related disciplines. 
  • Strong understanding of core security principles including identity and access management; authentication and authorization; network security; cryptography and key management; data protection and privacy; security monitoring and incident response; and secure software development. 
  • Experience assessing and securing cloud-native architectures. 
  • Strong knowledge of Kubernetes, container security, service-to-service communications, workload isolation, and modern application deployment patterns. 
  • Experience with one or more major cloud providers: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). 
  • Experience conducting threat modeling using frameworks such as STRIDE, ATT&CK, PASTA, or similar methodologies. 
  • Ability to build and communicate architecture diagrams that clearly articulate data flows, trust boundaries, security controls, and deployment models. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage audiences ranging from engineers to CISOs. 
  • Experience presenting security recommendations and architectural guidance to customers and executive stakeholders. 
  • A curious mindset and willingness to continuously learn emerging technologies including AI, cloud-native platforms, and modern security architectures. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience supporting Fortune 500 or highly regulated enterprise customers. 
  • Experience working with financial services, healthcare, or public sector organizations. 
  • Knowledge of AI security, AI governance, model risk management, prompt injection risks, agentic systems, and emerging AI threats. 
  • Experience using AI technologies to improve security operations, threat detection, security analysis, or engineering productivity. 
  • Familiarity with JavaScript, scripting, or automation development. 
  • Experience with the ServiceNow platform. 
  • Experience developing security reference architectures, implementation patterns, or technical guidance consumed at scale. 
  • Industry certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, Azure Security Engineer, GSEC, GIAC, OSCP, or equivalent. 

Why This Role Is Unique 

This role sits at the intersection of customer engagement, security engineering, cloud architecture, and AI security. You'll help some of the world's largest organizations make security decisions that directly influence platform adoption, AI strategy, and enterprise risk management. 

You'll have the opportunity to shape product direction, influence engineering roadmaps, develop industry-leading security architectures, and help define how ServiceNow brings secure AI and cloud-native innovation to the world's most demanding customers.

Job Description

Role summary 

The senior technical architect, infrastructure and cloud sets direction for how our corporate and cloud infrastructure evolves to support secure, reliable, scalable, and cost-effective business services. As part of the technical architecture team, this role connects infrastructure and cloud decisions to enterprise architecture and the broader technology roadmap. The role researches new technologies, advises on current solutions, and drives improvement, including upgrades, retirements, and replacements. This is a senior individual contributor role that sets direction through standards, roadmaps, guardrails, and architecture decisions. 

 What you get to do in this role:

  • Help define the current-state, transition-state, and target-state infrastructure and cloud architecture, with a multiyear roadmap tied to business priorities, risk, lifecycle, capacity, and cost. Help align that direction with enterprise architecture principles and the broader technology roadmap, and surface dependencies that affect enterprise plans. 

  • Establish reference architectures, principles, standards, and patterns across cloud, data center, networking, compute, storage, containers, and backup. Advise on infrastructure as code and policy as code, and support delivery teams in adopting them. 

  • Help define cloud governance, standards, and architectural guardrails for Azure and GCP, including account and subscription structure, landing zones, cost controls, and policy as code. Advise teams on operating within them, and surface where a guardrail needs to change. 

  • Lead infrastructure architecture reviews and provide architecture input on major technical decisions. Help scope proofs of concept and vendor evaluations. Evaluate options, document tradeoffs, risks, and value, fit, operability, and total cost, and help drive decisions to closure with accountable stakeholders. 

  • Recommend resilience and compliance requirements for high availability, disaster recovery, backup and recovery, and continuity, and help align recovery objectives with business criticality. 

  • Partner with Security Architecture on resilience, compliance, and zero-trust, so that security requirements are built into infrastructure and cloud standards from the start. 

  • Look ahead to AI and ML infrastructure needs, including compute capacity, specialized hardware, data storage, and hybrid hosting. Understand the agentic AI patterns, such as RAG, A2A, and MCP, that shape those needs. Research emerging technologies that could change how we build and run infrastructure, and advise on when to adopt them. 

  • Default to out-of-the-box capabilities. Recommend a documented case for any custom pattern or exception and advise on retiring custom solutions where a standard capability will do. 

  • Support and collaborate regularly with the DT Integration, Core Systems, and Product teams to align infrastructure needs, dependencies, and roadmaps. Advise these teams on the infrastructure implications of their integration, core system, and product decisions, and help plan changes that depend on shared infrastructure. 

  • Partner with finance and operations to inform infrastructure economics through capacity planning, lifecycle management, workload placement, and FinOps practices. Draw on incidents, capacity trends, audit findings, and resilience test results to inform standards and roadmaps. 

  • Represent infrastructure and cloud in the architecture team and its governance forums, including the Architecture Review Board. Build trusted relationships with senior technology and business leaders, and mentor architects and engineers. 

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in infrastructure, cloud, platform engineering, or systems engineering, including substantial architecture responsibility for complex enterprise environments. 

  • Demonstrated success defining infrastructure and cloud strategy and roadmaps that span multiple technology domains and delivery teams. 

  • Deep expertise in several infrastructure domains, with enough breadth to make integrated decisions across cloud, network, compute, storage, resilience, and cost. 

  • Strong working knowledge of Azure and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) architecture, including landing zones, connectivity, identity dependencies, workload placement, and shared-responsibility models. 

  • Solid understanding of agentic AI concepts and patterns, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent-to-agent (A2A) communication, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and related technologies. 

  • Experience integrating disparate systems, with a strong understanding of enterprise integration patterns, such as APIs, messaging, and event-driven architecture. 

  • Experience defining cloud governance, guardrails, and standards in a large enterprise, and getting teams to adopt them. 

  • Experience creating and governing reference architectures, standards, and architecture decision records. 

  • Working knowledge of infrastructure as code and modern automation practices. 

  • Ability to evaluate architecture choices on business value, risk, cost, and operational evidence, not technology preference. 

  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and technical teams without relying on direct authority. 

  • Clear written and verbal communication for both engineering and executive audiences. 

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience. 

  • Preferred qualifications 

  • Experience in a large, global, regulated, or mission-critical environment. 

  • Familiarity with IT service management practices, including the IT Infrastructure Library (ITIL), and with configuration management database (CMDB) alignment for infrastructure configuration items. 

  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks, such as TOGAF or COBIT, or equivalent. 

  • Experience with release planning using Agile and Scrum practices.

Job Description

Role Overview:

As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer supporting our Canada Protected B regulated cloud environment, you will provide senior technical leadership for the reliability, availability, scalability, security, and performance of critical cloud infrastructure and services.

In addition to personally solving complex production problems, you will provide technical leadership across systems, services, and engineering teams. You will take ownership of ambiguous, multi-system reliability problems, influence technical architecture and operational standards, lead significant engineering and automation initiatives, and help other engineers solve difficult problems.

The Staff Site Reliability Engineer is an individual-contributor technical leadership role. Success is measured not only by the problems you personally solve, but by your ability to improve the reliability and operability of the broader environment, influence technical direction, reduce systemic operational risk, and increase the effectiveness of other engineers and partner teams.

Canada Protected B Eligibility:

Due to Government of Canada regulatory requirements, this position requires the successful completion of a Government of Canada Reliability Status screening as a condition of employment. The screening process requires 5 years of verifiable background history. This includes identity verification, education verification, a criminal record check, and a credit check. Candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain Reliability Status, which generally requires Canadian citizenship or Canadian permanent resident status.  Employment is contingent upon successful completion and maintenance of the required screening.

Work Schedule:

This position is part of a 24x5 Site Reliability Engineering operation supporting the Canada Protected B regulated environment. Engineers will be assigned to a fixed day, swing, or overnight shift designed to provide continuous operational coverage Monday through Friday.

Each shift includes eight hours of scheduled work and a one-hour unpaid meal period. Adjacent shifts overlap by one hour to enable structured warm handovers, continuity of active incident response, and transfer of operational context.

  • Day Shift: 7:00 AM - 4:00 PM ET
  • Swing Shift: 3:00 PM - 12:00 AM ET
  • Overnight Shift: 11:00 PM - 8:00 AM ET

Shift assignments and schedules may be adjusted based on operational coverage requirements. Meal periods will be scheduled outside the warm-handover window and coordinated to maintain operational coverage.

What you get to do in this role:

  • Provide technical leadership during complex, high-impact production incidents spanning multiple services, systems, or technology domains.
  • Lead technical Root Cause Analysis (RCA) for significant or complex incidents and drive systemic corrective and preventative actions across services and teams.
  • Identify recurring and systemic reliability risks and lead engineering initiatives that address their underlying technical causes.
  • Lead cross-functional reliability initiatives involving SRE, application engineering, infrastructure, networking, database, cloud, and security teams.
  • Influence technical architecture and engineering approaches for reliability, scalability, automation, observability, operational readiness, and production supportability.
  • Design and lead automation initiatives that eliminate significant sources of operational toil and create scalable, reusable solutions across services or environments.
  • Develop and guide operational tooling and automation using Bash, Python, and/or JavaScript, including reusable tools and frameworks that improve the effectiveness of other engineers.
  • Provide deep technical leadership across Linux, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, networking, databases, configuration management, and distributed production systems.
  • Design and improve infrastructure and configuration automation using Ansible and Puppet, scripting, APIs, and related infrastructure-management technologies.
  • Lead the operation, troubleshooting, and reliability improvement of Kubernetes and containerized production environments.
  • Lead complex database troubleshooting, performance, and reliability improvements, particularly for PostgreSQL environments; MariaDB/MySQL experience is also applicable.
  • Establish and promote effective Git-based engineering practices for infrastructure, configuration, and automation code.
  • Diagnose complex network and distributed-system issues involving TCP/IP, DNS, IP addressing, routing, load balancing, connectivity, and network security technologies.
  • Drive improvements to monitoring, observability, service health, and operational readiness across multiple systems and services.
  • Evaluate proposed technical designs for reliability, scalability, failure modes, and operational risks and influence engineering decisions before systems reach production.
  • Establish, improve, and promote SRE engineering practices and operational standards across teams.
  • Mentor engineers through technical problem solving, incident response, design reviews, automation, troubleshooting, and reliability engineering practices.
  • Communicate complex technical issues, engineering decisions, systemic risks, and recommendations clearly to engineering teams, stakeholders, and leadership.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 8+ years Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field; or 6 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years experience; or equivalent/relevant engineering work experience, with demonstrated ability to independently own and resolve complex production and reliability problems.
  • Extensive experience administering, troubleshooting, and engineering Linux-based production environments at scale.
  • Advanced scripting and automation experience using Bash, Python, and/or JavaScript, including designing reusable automation and engineering solutions leveraged by other engineers or teams.
  • Significant experience engineering and operating cloud infrastructure, with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) preferred.
  • Strong hands-on experience designing and implementing infrastructure and configuration management automation using Ansible and Puppet.
  • Strong experience operating, troubleshooting, designing, and improving Kubernetes and containerized production environments.
  • Strong command of Git-based engineering workflows, including source-controlled infrastructure, configuration, and automation.
  • Deep database administration, performance, and troubleshooting experience, preferably with PostgreSQL; MariaDB/MySQL expertise is also applicable.
  • Advanced networking knowledge, including TCP/IP, DNS, IP addressing, routing, load balancing, connectivity troubleshooting, and network security concepts.
  • Significant experience leading major incident management and Root Cause Analysis, including driving systemic corrective actions and preventative engineering work.
  • Deep experience with monitoring and observability across applications, services, infrastructure, databases, and networks.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives spanning multiple systems, technology domains, or engineering teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, cross-domain technical problems where the solution is not already defined.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical architecture, engineering practices, reliability standards, and operational design beyond an individual service or system.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and raising the technical effectiveness of the broader engineering organization.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly communicate complex technical decisions, tradeoffs, and risks to engineering teams and leadership.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Job Description

As a Sales Coach, you will work one on one with sellers to lift pipeline generation, deal quality, and forecast accuracy. This is a hands-on field coaching role. You will spend most of your week with sellers and in live deal work, and the rest building the programs that scale what works. You report to the manager of the department and partner closely with frontline sales managers, enablement, product marketing, and the teams integrating newly acquired sellers.

What you get to do in this role:

Coach sellers one on one - This is the center of the role. You will spend most of your week with individual sellers, working on whatever stands between them and their number.

● Run a recurring one-on-one coaching cadence with each assigned seller against a written individual development plan

● Coach the full seller motion—prospecting and outbound rigor, territory and account management, deal management and qualification, executive presence, time and calendar management, CRM accuracy and forecast hygiene, and personal change management through reorgs and portfolio shifts

● Facilitate role plays and certification checkpoints across discovery, executive conversations, pricing, objection handling, and competitive positioning, so mastery is demonstrated rather than assumed

● Observe live customer calls and give same-day feedback that names the specific behavior to change

Build coaching programs with your manager

● Partner with your manager to design programs that answer real business needs—segment ramp paths, focused skill sprints, manager coaching enablement, and remediation tracks

● Build segment-appropriate variants where Enterprise and Commercial need different treatment of the same skill—multi-stakeholder pursuit strategy and executive alignment on one side, call volume, cycle discipline, and portfolio juggling on the other

● Design coaching that scales across a large Commercial population without losing the personal quality that makes coaching work

● Contribute reusable assets back to the global library: playbooks, call frameworks, role play scenarios, and certification rubrics

● Pilot, measure, and retire—keep what moves the number and cut what does not

Support large-scale training events

● Help design and deliver org-wide moments: sales kickoff, bootcamps, mid-year kickoffs, product launch enablement, and field readiness days

● Own assigned tracks end to end—content, facilitators, breakout design, certification, and the reinforcement plan that follows

● Build the follow-through so event content shows up in seller behavior 30 and 60 days later

Document and report progress

● Build and maintain the documentation layer that makes coaching visible and auditable—rep scorecards, skill matrices, certification records, development plans, and progress over time

● Report coaching impact to sales and enablement leadership on a set cadence, tied to business results rather than activity counts

● Keep records consistent enough that another coach could pick up any rep and know exactly where they stand

Shorten time to productivity for new hires, transfers, and acquired teams

● Own the coaching side of ramp for new hires, internal transfers, and sellers joining through acquisition, with an explicit goal of moving time to productivity from roughly six months to three

● Build and run acquisition-specific enablement: cross-portfolio positioning, joint account mapping, tooling and process conversion, and the cultural onboarding that makes acquired sellers feel like part of the team quickly

● Track ramp milestones by cohort and flag an at-risk ramp early enough to fix it

● Give hiring managers a clear read on where each new seller stands and what they need next

Validate readiness on new products, releases, and acquisitions

● Assess whether sellers are genuinely equipped to sell new products, new releases, and newly acquired portfolios—measured through certification, call review, and pipeline evidence, not attendance

● Report readiness gaps to product, marketing, and enablement partners with a recommended fix and a date

● Re-test after remediation and close the loop

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

● Seven or more years in enterprise or commercial software sales, sales management, or sales coaching and enablement

● Direct experience with both a large-deal Enterprise motion and a higher-velocity Commercial or mid-market motion, and a clear point of view on how coaching differs between them

● A track record of coaching adults to behavior change—specific sellers or teams who improved on a measurable metric because of your work

● Fluency in at least one recognized sales methodology, such as MEDDICC, Challenger, Strategic Selling, or Command of the Message, and the ability to coach to it rather than just describe it

● Strong CRM discipline—you can inspect a pipeline and tell the difference between a data problem and a deal problem

● Comfort with the enablement stack: CRM, conversation intelligence, sales content management, and a learning management system

● Credibility with senior sellers and frontline managers—this role carries influence, not authority

● Excellent facilitation and written communication skills, and the judgment to know when to teach and when to ask

Nice to Have:

● Prior quota-carrying experience at both Enterprise and Commercial

● Experience coaching across a multi-product or platform portfolio

● Formal coaching certification, such as ICF or equivalent

● Experience integrating an acquired sales team

You will take ownership of ambiguous, multi-system reliability problems, influence technical architecture and operational standards, lead significant engineering and automation initiatives, and help other engineers solve difficult problems.

The Staff Site Reliability Engineer is an individual-contributor technical leadership role. Success is measured not only by the problems you personally solve, but by your ability to improve the reliability and operability of the broader environment, influence technical direction, reduce systemic operational risk, and increase the effectiveness of other engineers and partner teams.

Canada Protected B Eligibility:

Due to Government of Canada regulatory requirements, this position requires the successful completion of a Government of Canada Reliability Status screening as a condition of employment. The screening process requires 5 years of verifiable background history. This includes identity verification, education verification, a criminal record check, and a credit check. Candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain Reliability Status, which generally requires Canadian citizenship or Canadian permanent resident status.  Employment is contingent upon successful completion and maintenance of the required screening.

Work Schedule:

This position is part of a shift-based Site Reliability Engineering operation supporting the Canada Protected B regulated environment. The initial operating model provides continuous 24x5 coverage through fixed day, swing, and overnight shifts, Monday through Friday.

Each shift includes eight hours of scheduled work and a one-hour unpaid meal period. Adjacent shifts overlap by one hour to support structured warm handovers and continuity of active incident response.

  • Day Shift: 7:00 AM - 4:00 PM ET
  • Swing Shift: 3:00 PM - 12:00 AM ET
  • Overnight Shift: 11:00 PM - 8:00 AM ET

Engineers will participate in an on-call rotation that may include nights, weekends, and holidays. As operational requirements evolve, schedules may change to include alternative workweeks, regular weekend coverage, or other day, swing, and overnight assignments. Meal periods will be scheduled outside the warm-handover window and coordinated to maintain operational coverage.

What you get to do in this role:

  • Provide technical leadership during complex, high-impact production incidents spanning multiple services, systems, or technology domains.
  • Lead technical Root Cause Analysis (RCA) for significant or complex incidents and drive systemic corrective and preventative actions across services and teams.
  • Identify recurring and systemic reliability risks and lead engineering initiatives that address their underlying technical causes.
  • Lead cross-functional reliability initiatives involving SRE, application engineering, infrastructure, networking, database, cloud, and security teams.
  • Influence technical architecture and engineering approaches for reliability, scalability, automation, observability, operational readiness, and production supportability.
  • Design and lead automation initiatives that eliminate significant sources of operational toil and create scalable, reusable solutions across services or environments.
  • Develop and guide operational tooling and automation using Bash, Python, and/or JavaScript, including reusable tools and frameworks that improve the effectiveness of other engineers.
  • Provide deep technical leadership across Linux, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, networking, databases, configuration management, and distributed production systems.
  • Design and improve infrastructure and configuration automation using Ansible and Puppet, scripting, APIs, and related infrastructure-management technologies.
  • Lead the operation, troubleshooting, and reliability improvement of Kubernetes and containerized production environments.
  • Lead complex database troubleshooting, performance, and reliability improvements, particularly for PostgreSQL environments; MariaDB/MySQL experience is also applicable.
  • Establish and promote effective Git-based engineering practices for infrastructure, configuration, and automation code.
  • Diagnose complex network and distributed-system issues involving TCP/IP, DNS, IP addressing, routing, load balancing, connectivity, and network security technologies.
  • Drive improvements to monitoring, observability, service health, and operational readiness across multiple systems and services.
  • Evaluate proposed technical designs for reliability, scalability, failure modes, and operational risks and influence engineering decisions before systems reach production.
  • Establish, improve, and promote SRE engineering practices and operational standards across teams.
  • Mentor engineers through technical problem solving, incident response, design reviews, automation, troubleshooting, and reliability engineering practices.
  • Communicate complex technical issues, engineering decisions, systemic risks, and recommendations clearly to engineering teams, stakeholders, and leadership.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
  • 8+ years Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field; or 6 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years experience; or equivalent/relevant engineering work experience, with demonstrated ability to independently own and resolve complex production and reliability problems.
  • Extensive experience administering, troubleshooting, and engineering Linux-based production environments at scale.
  • Advanced scripting and automation experience using Bash, Python, and/or JavaScript, including designing reusable automation and engineering solutions leveraged by other engineers or teams.
  • Significant experience engineering and operating cloud infrastructure, with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) preferred.
  • Strong hands-on experience designing and implementing infrastructure and configuration management automation using Ansible and Puppet.
  • Strong experience operating, troubleshooting, designing, and improving Kubernetes and containerized production environments.
  • Strong command of Git-based engineering workflows, including source-controlled infrastructure, configuration, and automation.
  • Deep database administration, performance, and troubleshooting experience, preferably with PostgreSQL; MariaDB/MySQL expertise is also applicable.
  • Advanced networking knowledge, including TCP/IP, DNS, IP addressing, routing, load balancing, connectivity troubleshooting, and network security concepts.
  • Significant experience leading major incident management and Root Cause Analysis, including driving systemic corrective actions and preventative engineering work.
  • Deep experience with monitoring and observability across applications, services, infrastructure, databases, and networks.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives spanning multiple systems, technology domains, or engineering teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, cross-domain technical problems where the solution is not already defined.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence technical architecture, engineering practices, reliability standards, and operational design beyond an individual service or system.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and raising the technical effectiveness of the broader engineering organization.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly communicate complex technical decisions, tradeoffs, and risks to engineering teams and leadership.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Agentic Platform - Moveworks
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Who we are

Moveworks is the Agentic AI Assistant platform that empowers the entire workforce. 

Our platform enables employees to converse with all of their business systems through natural language to quickly find answers and automate tasks. Powered by the world's most advanced LLMs, our proprietary models, and a sophisticated Agentic AI platform, we're transforming how work gets done by allowing AI to take initiative, streamline complex workflows, and continuously learn and adapt.

Moveworks is trusted by over 5.5 million employees at more than 350 of the world’s largest companies, including 10% of the Fortune 500, to automate everyday tasks and streamline business operations. Recognized on the Forbes Cloud 100 and AI 50 lists, Moveworks was also named one of Fast Company’s 2025 Most Innovative Companies and Inc’s Best in Business, in the Best in Innovation category. Moveworks was also recognized at Microsoft’s 2025 Partner of the Year and in 2024, received the AI Breakthrough Award. 

In December 2025, Moveworks was acquired by ServiceNow, marking a pivotal milestone in our journey to create a single front door to work for all business systems. By combining ServiceNow’s leading workflow automation with Moveworks’ Reasoning Engine and natural language capabilities, we deliver the AI platform for every person and every workflow. Built to go beyond basic summaries to deliver meaningful business impact. Together, our AI acts across enterprise systems to turn conversations into completed work.

By joining our team, you’ll be at the forefront of the AI transformation, backed by the global scale of ServiceNow and the agility of a high-growth company. We are looking for world-class talent to help us extend agentic AI to every employee across every corner of the business. 

Come join us!

ServiceNow

It all started in sunny San Diego, California in 2004 when a visionary engineer, Fred Luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. Fast forward to today — ServiceNow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative AI-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. But this is just the beginning of our journey. Join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone.

Job Description

The Role

We're building the runtime infrastructure that powers Moveworks' AI agents — the systems that orchestrate, execute, and deliver agent responses to millions of enterprise users in real time. This role sits where large language models meet distributed systems. You'll apply machine learning, LLM, and distributed systems expertise to make agents plan, reason, and use tools reliably, and you'll build the production systems that run those agents at enterprise scale.

Our AI agents can plan, execute multi-step workflows, call tools, wait on human input, and resume — all while maintaining correctness, observability, and low latency. The systems that make this possible are what you'll build and own.


What you get to do in this role:

  • Agent orchestration engine — A state machine that manages long-running agent sessions, coordinating planning, execution, and user interaction across multiple LLM calls and tool invocations
  • Model routing and adaptation — Choose, route between, and fine-tune or distill LLMs for specific agent tasks. Meet enterprise requirements such as granular permissions, data freshness, explainability, and preserving general knowledge.
  • Distributed session management — Lease-based ownership using conditional writes, heartbeat protocols, and crash recovery via checkpointing
  • Event-driven message pipeline — FIFO queues for ordered delivery, consumers for event processing, and real-time streaming via gRPC and Socket.IO
  • Structured concurrency — Running multiple concurrent tasks per session with fail-fast semantics and graceful cancellation
  • Observability infrastructure — OpenTelemetry instrumentation, distributed trace context propagation across async boundaries, custom span lifecycle management for sessions that span minutes
  • Caching and state layers — Redis, DynamoDB KV stores with per-org/per-bot scoping, batch read optimization, and hot-reload configuration
  • Tool and agent connectivity for LLMs: Build MCP and agent-to-agent (A2A) capabilities, including tool discovery, namespacing, and tool selection over large tool catalogs, so the LLM picks and calls the right tool from thousands of candidates.
  • Token efficiency and context engineering — Lower the agent's cost and latency through prompt and context discipline, caching, speculative and parallel model-call scheduling, and reducing tokens spent across multi-step LLM reasoning chains.
  • Open-weights model adoption and evaluation — Quickly stand up newly released open-weights LLMs at different quantization levels, run them in a test environment, and benchmark their accuracy, latency and cost on agent tasks. Use the results to decide which models reach production.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

You should have deep experience in at least 3 of these areas:

  • Distributed systems: consistency models, idempotency, exactly-once delivery, distributed locking/leasing
  • Concurrent/async programming: Python asyncio, Go goroutines, structured concurrency, cancellation handling
  • Event-driven architectures: message queues (SQS, Kafka), pub/sub, backpressure, delivery guarantees
  • Database systems for infrastructure: DynamoDB (conditional writes, transactions), Redis (connection pooling, pub/sub)
  • Observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, span context propagation, Prometheus metrics
  • gRPC/protobuf: streaming RPCs, service interface design, error handling patterns
  • Machine learning: Large language models, natural language processing, LLM evaluation



Required:

  • 5+ years building production backend/infrastructure systems
  • Strong in Python or Go (ideally both)
  • Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale
  • Hands-on experience building production systems that use LLMs or other ML models
  • Comfort with ambiguity — these are novel problems without textbook solutions



Relevant past experience:

  • Building and shipping products on large language models with techniques such as RAG, chain-of-thought, self-reflection, tool and function calling, and agentic reasoning.
  • Training, fine-tuning, or evaluating machine learning models on large datasets in production, especially for NLP, retrieval, or ranking.
  • Improving relevance or quality through careful experimentation: designing metrics, building evaluation datasets, and developing new features and signals for ranking or model selection.
  • Research or applied work in machine learning, LLMs, agentic systems, information retrieval, or ranking and relevance.

  • Build frameworks to monitor pricing performance and present insights and recommendations to senior leadership.

  • Lead pricing research, including competitor analysis and market benchmarking, to keep EmployeeWorks competitively positioned.

You will help shape how we build AI-native products and establish the technical foundation for the next generation of intelligent enterprise applications.

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Job Description

The Role
As a Distinguished Engineer in HRSD, you set the technical direction for model-driven capability across the HR domain, the agentic and conversational experiences that interpret employee, manager, and HR agent intent, reason over profile, case, catalog, policy, and knowledge context, and act on the user's behalf. Your unit of ownership is the architecture, standards, and evaluation infrastructure that let multiple teams ship those experiences safely — not a single feature set.

This is not an ML research role; you do not train foundation models. It is also distinct from traditional full-stack staff work, where systems follow deterministic logic. Two things shape the job: much of the load-bearing logic lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, context, tool descriptions, guardrails — and must be engineered with the same discipline as code; and because behavior is probabilistic, correctness is established through evaluation at scale, not fixed assertions.

What You'll Own

  • AI architecture for the domain. How agents are decomposed and composed, where reasoning happens, how context is assembled and bounded, how tools are exposed, and how autonomy is delegated. Own the multi-release calls: model selection and migration, orchestration approach, build-versus-adopt, and the cost/latency/quality tradeoffs behind each.
  • The autonomy boundary. Decide as domain policy which HR actions an agent may take, which require a human decision point, and which no agent should attempt. Anything changing pay, employment status, restricted records, or employee-relations matters requires a human in the path by construction — build the mechanisms that make those constraints structural.
  • The shared instruction and tool description surface. HRSD ships as product; customers configure, extend, and override this surface on their own instances. Treat it as a versioned contract with upgrade-safe extension points, deprecation paths, and compatibility guarantees.
  • Evaluation as infrastructure. Own the golden datasets, multi-turn suites, judge calibration, CI gates, and drift detection that let teams change behavior safely. Extend coverage to HR-specific failure classes: access-boundary violations, cross-scope leakage, jurisdictional and policy-variant correctness.
  • Production quality and safety. Observability for containment, hallucination rate, tool-selection error, unsafe action, and injection vectors from user-supplied content entering agent context. Because HR conversation content is itself restricted, design diagnosis that works without exposing what was said.
  • AI-assisted engineering standards. Convert ambiguous problems into testable specs; define what accountable agent-assisted delivery looks like for the domain — specification standards, review expectations, verification harnesses — and hold the line on it.
  • Hands-on where it matters. The hard integration, the risky migration, the prototype that settles an architectural argument, the incident nobody else can unblock.
  • Partner across functions. Collaborate efficiently with product, engineering, design to co-create scalable AI solutions and translate business needs into robust technical designs.

Qualifications

What You Bring

  • 13+ years of software engineering, with a record of technical direction adopted beyond your immediate team.
  • Direct, hands-on experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing autonomous workflows, and building the evaluation that verifies them.
  • Production experience with LLM APIs, retrieval-grounded features, agent orchestration, tool and function calling, and structured output enforcement — including at least one model or orchestration migration carried through production.
  • Entitlement-aware data handling: per-user access enforcement in retrieval and tool layers, scope separation between roles, and handling of restricted records under audit.
  • Evaluation experience used by engineers other than yourself: dataset curation, judge calibration, CI gating, drift detection.
  • Strong command of system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing across front-end, server-side, and relational data work with a high quality mindset.
  • Effective, accountable use of AI coding assistants and agents.
  • On-call and incident-command experience on customer-facing systems, including ownership of the systemic fixes that followed.
  • Experience in software stack including Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, React and demonstrated ability to quickly learn new tools and frameworks.
  • Bachelor's degree in CS, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

  • HR domain depth: case management, employee journey and lifecycle, or payroll/benefits/leave/absence sufficient to set requirements.
  • Integration with core HR, payroll, or benefits systems of record, including reconciliation and eventual-consistency patterns.
  • Contribution in a Forward deployment model to champion customer adoption.

Company Description

Job Description

ServiceNow is seeking a Partner Technology Architect — Autonomous Workforce to drive partner growth across the AI-powered workflows that run the modern enterprise — IT service and operations management, employee experience, and strategic portfolio execution. This is a senior technical strategist role that combines deep technical expertise in ServiceNow ITSM, ITOM, HR Service Delivery (HRSD), and Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) with business acumen, partner activation at scale, and the ability to translate complex service-operations and employee-experience requirements into commercially viable solutions. As a Practice-aligned Partner Technology Architect within the Autonomous Workforce Practice, you will be engaged where deep IT, operations, and employee workflow expertise is required — working alongside partner-aligned Partner Technology Architects and Partner Solution Engineers.

The Autonomous Workforce Practice sits at the core of ServiceNow’s platform — the workflows where AI agents, automation, and human teams operate together to run IT and serve employees at scale. This role helps partners move beyond traditional, ticket-driven service models to an AI-native operating model where work is detected, routed, and resolved autonomously, ensuring partners can confidently position, build, and deliver differentiated solutions that displace legacy platforms and drive measurable operational outcomes.

What You’ll Do

As a Partner Technology Architect — Autonomous Workforce, you will serve as the go-to IT, operations, and employee workflow expert across the partner ecosystem, driving technical excellence, competitive differentiation, and commercial success for autonomous-workforce partner solutions.

Autonomous Workforce Co-Innovation & Technology Strategy

  • Co-create autonomous-operations architectures with partners, developing reference architectures for IT Service Management (ITSM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), HR Service Delivery (HRSD), Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM), and industry-specific operational workflows.
  • Drive collaborative adoption of AI-enhanced capabilities including AI Agents for employee and IT self-service, autonomous incident resolution, predictive operations and AIOps analytics, and automated change and remediation.
  • Build reusable co-innovation assets including solution templates, industry-specific accelerators, demo environments, and operational workflow blueprints.
  • Provide specialized expertise in employee experience architectures, including Employee Center design, virtual agent configuration, and cross-workflow orchestration across IT, HR, and operations.
  • Influence ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, and SPM product architecture and roadmap based on partner ecosystem needs; represent partner voice in internal Autonomous Workforce strategy forums.

Pipeline & Revenue Growth

  • Lead technical workshops with partners and engage directly with CIO, VP of IT Operations, and CHRO stakeholders to co-design autonomous-workforce solutions.
  • Execute strategic proofs of concept demonstrating incident and ticket reduction, deflection, operational cost reduction, and employee productivity acceleration.
  • Guide partners on competitive positioning against legacy ITSM and ITOM platforms (BMC Helix, Atlassian Jira Service Management, Ivanti, Microsoft) and articulate ServiceNow’s AI-native, single-platform differentiation.
  • Present ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, and SPM architecture and industry-specific operational strategies to executive audiences.

Partner Enablement & Ecosystem Scale

  • Design and deliver comprehensive Autonomous Workforce architecture training programs, workshops, and executive briefings that build lasting partner capability.
  • Mentor partner architects and pre-sales teams on ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, and SPM solution positioning, competitive differentiation, and industry-specific operational patterns.
  • Assess partner technical capabilities across IT and employee workflows and identify gaps; develop practice-specific capability maturation plans and certification pathways.
  • Represent ServiceNow Autonomous Workforce innovation at industry events and IT and HR transformation forums; contribute to thought leadership content.

Business Growth & Value Realization

  • Collaborate with partner-aligned Partner Technology Architects on Autonomous Workforce joint business planning.
  • Guide partners from concept to validated solution to scalable commercialization with clear monetization pathways.
  • Connect operational architecture to measurable business outcomes (mean time to resolution, deflection rate, operational cost reduction, employee productivity).

Autonomous Workforce Market Intelligence & Competitive Strategy

  • Maintain expert-level knowledge of the ITSM, ITOM, and employee-service landscape including BMC Helix, Atlassian Jira Service Management, Ivanti, Microsoft, Freshservice, and emerging platforms.
  • Advise partners on coexistence and migration strategies for customers transitioning from legacy ITSM and ITOM platforms.
  • Monitor industry-specific adoption patterns across IT and employee workflows and translate market intelligence into partner-relevant insights.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

Required:

  • 8+ years pre-sales, solution architecture, or technical consulting experience with proven success in ITSM, ITOM, employee experience, or enterprise service management solutions.
  • 5+ years deep domain expertise in IT service management, IT operations, HR service delivery, or enterprise workflow automation platforms.
  • Expert-level knowledge of service and operations architectures including incident, problem, and change management, CMDB/CSDM, event management and AIOps, knowledge management, and employee self-service.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the competitive landscape including BMC, Atlassian, Ivanti, Microsoft, and emerging enterprise service management platforms.
  • Deep expertise in IT or employee experience transformation for at least two industry verticals (e.g., Financial Services, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Telecommunications, Public Sector).
  • Proven experience engaging with CIO, IT operations, and CHRO executives and articulating operational transformation strategies to diverse audiences.
  • Experience working with partner ecosystems (GSIs, SIs, ISVs) and understanding partner business models and co-selling dynamics.
  • Working knowledge of AI-enabled operations use cases including virtual agents, autonomous incident resolution, predictive analytics, AIOps, and automated remediation workflows.
  • Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving.
  • Travel for partner, customer, and organizational activities up to 25%.

What This Role Does Not Do

Perform platform configuration, development, or solution delivery. Own commercial contracts, pricing, or financial program management.
